examplePolite.ja: 彼は絶対モテますよね。
examplePolite.english: I bet he's really popular with girls.

blocks.label: Leaving it to someone
blocks.rationale: Lets you hand a job or choice to someone, or lean on them.
blocks.interference: Makaseru hands over a task, tayoru leans on a person; suki ni shite can sound cold.

items.use: 'Makasete!' means 'Leave it to me!'; 'Makaseru yo' hands a decision to the other person.

example.ja: 料理は私に任せて。
example.english: Leave the cooking to me.

examplePolite.romaji: ryouri wa watashi ni makasete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 料理は私に任せてください。
examplePolite.english: Please leave the cooking to me.

items.notes: The person who takes the job gets ni: 'Kimi ni makaseru' means 'I'll leave it to you'.

items.english: leaving it to someone; chef's choice
items.use: Used as 'omakase suru' or 'omakase de' to hand over a choice; in restaurants, the chef's-choice menu.

example.ja: 色はお任せするよ。
example.english: I'll leave the colour up to you.

examplePolite.romaji: iro wa omakase shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 色はお任せします。
examplePolite.english: I'll leave the colour up to you.

items.notes: The polite face of makaseru; you use it about yourself handing over a choice.

items.english: rely on, depend on, count on
items.use: Often as 'Itsu demo tayotte ne' (you can always count on me).

example.ja: 困ったらいつでも頼ってね。
example.english: If you're ever stuck, you can always count on me.

examplePolite.romaji: komattara itsu demo tayotte kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 困ったらいつでも頼ってくださいね。
examplePolite.english: If you're ever stuck, you can always count on me.

items.notes: Don't mix up with tanomu (ask a favour); tayoru is leaning on someone.

items.use: 'Suki ni shite' can be a friendly 'go ahead' or an annoyed 'whatever, do what you want', depending on tone.

example.romaji: ato wa suki ni shite ii yo.
example.ja: あとは好きにしていいよ。
example.english: After that, do whatever you like.

examplePolite.romaji: ato wa suki ni shite ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あとは好きにしていいですよ。
examplePolite.english: After that, feel free to do whatever you like.

items.notes: Said flatly in an argument, it sounds cold.

blocks.label: Trust and respect
blocks.rationale: Lets you say who you trust, respect and admire.
blocks.interference: Shin'you trusts a word or record, shinrai a person; sonkei is respect, akogareru is admiring from afar.

items.use: Mostly shin'you dekiru / dekinai (can / can't trust) and 'Shin'you shite' (Trust me).

example.romaji: ano hito no koto, mada shin'you dekinai.
example.ja: あの人のこと、まだ信用できない。
example.english: I still can't trust that person.

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito no koto wa, mada shin'you dekimasen.
examplePolite.ja: あの人のことは、まだ信用できません。
examplePolite.english: I still can't trust that person.

items.notes: Shin'you is trusting someone's word or track record; shinrai is deeper trust in the person.

items.use: Deep trust in someone's character or ability, usually in -te iru.

example.romaji: kare no koto wa shinrai shiteru kara daijoubu.
example.ja: 彼のことは信頼してるから大丈夫。
example.english: I trust him, so it's fine.

examplePolite.romaji: kare no koto wa shinrai shite imasu kara, daijoubu desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼のことは信頼していますから、大丈夫です。
examplePolite.english: I trust him, so it's fine.

items.notes: The noun is common too: 'shinrai o ushinau' (lose someone's trust).

items.use: Usually in -te iru: 'sonkei shite iru'.

example.romaji: chichi no koto, hontou ni sonkei shiteru.
example.ja: 父のこと、本当に尊敬してる。
example.english: I really look up to my dad.

examplePolite.romaji: chichi no koto wa hontou ni sonkei shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 父のことは本当に尊敬しています。
examplePolite.english: I truly look up to my father.

items.notes: Sonkei is respect for someone you know; akogareru is admiring from a distance.

items.english: look up to, admire; long for
items.use: The person or thing takes ni; often a dream of being like someone or living somewhere.

example.romaji: kodomo no koro, pairotto ni akogareteta.
example.ja: 子供の頃、パイロットに憧れてた。
example.english: As a kid, I dreamed of being a pilot.

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo no koro, pairotto ni akogarete imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 子供の頃、パイロットに憧れていました。
examplePolite.english: As a child, I dreamed of being a pilot.

items.notes: The noun akogare is someone or something you dream of; it can be crush-like admiration.

blocks.label: Parties and groups
blocks.rationale: Covers joining in, getting loud, standing out and wrapping up a gathering.
blocks.interference: Kaisan ends a group or event, never a couple; that's wakareru.

items.use: The event takes ni: 'Nomikai ni sanka suru?' (Coming to the drinks?).

example.ja: 来週のパーティー、参加する？
example.english: Are you coming to next week's party?

examplePolite.romaji: raishuu no paatii ni sanka shimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 来週のパーティーに参加しますか？
examplePolite.english: Will you be joining next week's party?

items.notes: A bit formal; between friends, iku (go) often does the job.

items.use: For loud partying or a big fuss: 'Sawaganaide' (Keep it down / Don't make a fuss).

example.romaji: kinjo meiwaku da kara, sonna ni sawaganaide.
example.ja: 近所迷惑だから、そんなに騒がないで。
example.english: Don't make so much noise, you'll bother the neighbours.

examplePolite.romaji: kinjo meiwaku desu kara, sawaganaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 近所迷惑ですから、騒がないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please keep the noise down for the neighbours.

items.notes: The noun sawagi means a commotion or uproar.

items.use: For looks or behaviour that catches the eye.

example.romaji: sono akai fuku, sugoku medatsu ne.
example.ja: その赤い服、すごく目立つね。
example.english: That red outfit really stands out.

examplePolite.romaji: sono akai fuku, sugoku medachimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: その赤い服、すごく目立ちますね。
examplePolite.english: That red outfit really stands out.

items.notes: Medachitagari is a show-off who wants attention.

items.english: break up (a group); call it a day
items.use: Said at the end of a gathering, often alone: 'Jaa, kaisan!' (OK, everyone can head home). Also a band splitting up.

example.romaji: jaa, kyou wa kore de kaisan shiyou.
example.ja: じゃあ、今日はこれで解散しよう。
example.english: OK, let's call it a day here.

examplePolite.romaji: dewa, kyou wa kore de kaisan shimashou.
examplePolite.ja: では、今日はこれで解散しましょう。
examplePolite.english: Well, let's call it a day here.

items.notes: For a couple breaking up, use wakareru, not kaisan.

blocks.label: Go out, burn, flow, leak
blocks.rationale: Lets you describe lights going out, fire, and things flowing, leaking or slipping out.
blocks.interference: Kieru (it goes out) vs kesu (turn it off); moreru (leak) vs nagareru (flow).

items.use: Lights, fires and screens going off by themselves; also people or things vanishing.

example.ja: 急に電気が消えた。
example.english: The lights suddenly went out.

examplePolite.romaji: kyuu ni denki ga kiemashita.
examplePolite.ja: 急に電気が消えました。
examplePolite.english: The lights suddenly went out.

items.notes: Kesu is 'turn off, erase' (you do it): denki o kesu.

items.use: Things catching or being on fire; also feeling fired up.

example.romaji: moeru gomi wa getsuyoubi da yo.
example.ja: 燃えるゴミは月曜日だよ。
example.english: Burnable trash goes out on Mondays.

examplePolite.romaji: moeru gomi wa getsuyoubi desu.
examplePolite.ja: 燃えるゴミは月曜日です。
examplePolite.english: Burnable trash goes out on Mondays.

items.notes: Moyasu is 'burn it' (you do it). Moenai gomi = non-burnable trash.

items.english: come out (teeth, hair); slip out, leave (a meeting, group); go through
items.use: Something coming loose or out, or a person leaving partway: a meeting, a club, a job.

example.ja: ごめん、ちょっと抜けるね。
example.english: Sorry, I'm going to slip out for a bit.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, chotto nukemasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、ちょっと抜けます。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, I'll step out for a moment.

items.notes: Nuku is 'pull out, skip' (you do it): asagohan o nuku = skip breakfast.

items.use: Water, tears and time flowing; music playing in a shop; plans that get called off.

example.ja: 店でこの曲流れてた。
example.english: This song was playing in the shop.

examplePolite.romaji: mise de kono kyoku ga nagarete imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 店でこの曲が流れていました。
examplePolite.english: This song was playing in the shop.

items.notes: Nagasu is 'let flow' (you do it): toire o nagasu = flush the toilet.

items.english: leak; get out (secrets); be bursting (for the toilet)
items.use: Water, gas, light or secrets getting out; 'moresou!' is 'I'm bursting!'

example.ja: 天井から水が漏れてる。
example.english: Water's leaking from the ceiling.

examplePolite.romaji: tenjou kara mizu ga morete imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 天井から水が漏れています。
examplePolite.english: Water is leaking from the ceiling.

items.notes: Morasu is 'let leak' (you do it): himitsu o morasu = leak a secret.

blocks.label: More and less
blocks.rationale: Lets you say things go up or pile up, and turn things down or cut back.
blocks.interference: Fueru (it increases) vs fuyasu (increase it); tamaru (it piles up) vs tameru (save up).

items.english: increase; go up; grow in number
items.use: Numbers, weight, people or work going up by themselves.

example.ja: 最近体重が増えた。
example.english: I've put on weight lately.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin taijuu ga fuemashita.
examplePolite.ja: 最近体重が増えました。
examplePolite.english: I've put on weight lately.

items.notes: Fuyasu is 'increase it' (you do it). Opposite: heru, go down.

items.use: You make something go up: hours, staff, savings, friends.

example.ja: 来月からバイト増やす。
example.english: I'm taking more part-time shifts from next month.

examplePolite.romaji: raigetsu kara baito o fuyashimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 来月からバイトを増やします。
examplePolite.english: I'm taking on more part-time shifts from next month.

items.notes: Fueru is 'it increases' (by itself). Opposite: herasu, cut down.

items.english: pile up; build up; be saved up
items.use: Things building up you don't want (stress, dishes, work) or do want (money, points).

example.ja: 最近ストレスたまってる。
example.english: I've been so stressed lately.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin sutoresu ga tamatte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 最近ストレスがたまっています。
examplePolite.english: I've been under a lot of stress lately.

items.notes: Tameru is 'save up, let pile up' (you do it): okane o tameru.

items.english: lower; turn down; bring down; clear (plates)
items.use: Lowering volume, price, temperature or your head.

example.ja: ちょっと音下げて。
example.english: Turn the sound down a bit.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, chotto oto o sagete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、ちょっと音を下げてください。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, could you turn the sound down a little?

items.notes: Sagaru is 'go down' (by itself); opposite: ageru. Waiters ask 'osage shite yoroshii desu ka?' before clearing plates.

items.english: cut down on; hold back from; refrain
items.use: Cutting back on food, drink or habits; notices use it for a polite 'please don't'.

example.ja: 最近お酒控えてるんだ。
example.english: I'm cutting back on drinking these days.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin osake o hikaete imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 最近お酒を控えています。
examplePolite.english: I'm cutting back on alcohol these days.

items.notes: Signs say 'ohikae kudasai', please refrain.

blocks.label: Checking things
blocks.rationale: Lets you look things up, check, double-check and compare.
blocks.interference: kakunin suru, chekku suru and tashikameru all mean 'check'; shiraberu is finding out something new.

items.use: Making sure something is right or as planned: times, details, bookings.

example.ja: ちょっと確認してくるね。
example.english: I'll just go and check.

examplePolite.romaji: chotto kakunin shite kimasu.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっと確認してきます。
examplePolite.english: I'll just go and check.

items.notes: Also a noun: kakunin ga toreta (it's been confirmed).

items.use: Finding out something you don't know: online, in a dictionary, or by digging into it.

example.ja: ネットで調べてみるよ。
example.english: I'll look it up online.

examplePolite.romaji: netto de shirabete mimasu.
examplePolite.ja: ネットで調べてみます。
examplePolite.english: I'll look it up online.

items.notes: kakunin suru checks what you already think; shiraberu finds out something new.

items.use: Quick, casual checking of messages, mistakes or a list; also keeping an eye on something.

example.ja: 今朝のメール、チェックした？
example.english: Did you check this morning's email?

examplePolite.romaji: kesa no meeru wa chekku shimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今朝のメールはチェックしましたか？
examplePolite.english: Did you check this morning's email?

items.notes: Not for paying the bill; that's okaikei.

items.use: Seeing or trying it yourself to be sure something is true.

example.ja: 自分の目で確かめたい。
example.english: I want to see it for myself.

examplePolite.romaji: jibun no me de tashikametai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 自分の目で確かめたいです。
examplePolite.english: I want to see it for myself.

items.notes: Also for feelings: kimochi o tashikameru (find out how someone really feels).

items.use: X to Y o kuraberu (compare X and Y); X ni kurabete (compared with X).

example.romaji: hoka no mise to kurabete mita?
example.ja: ほかの店と比べてみた？
example.english: Did you compare it with other shops?

examplePolite.romaji: hoka no mise to kurabete mimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: ほかの店と比べてみましたか？
examplePolite.english: Did you compare it with other shops?

items.notes: hito to kurabenai de (don't compare yourself with others) is common advice.

blocks.label: Mistakes and do-overs
blocks.rationale: Lets you say something's wrong, you slipped up, you missed it, or you'll redo it.
blocks.interference: machigau (be wrong) gets mixed up with machigaeru (get X wrong).

items.use: Mostly as machigatteru or machigatta: it's wrong, you got it wrong.

example.ja: それ、ちょっと間違ってるよ。
example.english: That's a bit off.

examplePolite.romaji: sore, sukoshi machigatte imasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: それ、少し間違っていますよ。
examplePolite.english: That's a little off.

items.notes: To mix one thing up with another, use machigaeru: michi o machigaeta (I took a wrong turn). Noun: machigai.

items.use: Small slips, mainly at work, in games or in sport.

example.ja: ごめん、またミスしちゃった。
example.english: Sorry, I messed up again.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, mata misu shite shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、またミスしてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry, I made another mistake.

items.notes: Also a noun: ore no misu da (my mistake).

items.use: Doing something over from the start, from homework to a relationship.

example.ja: だめだ、もう一回やり直そう。
example.english: No good. Let's do it over.

examplePolite.romaji: dame desu ne, mou ikkai yarinaoshimashou.
examplePolite.ja: だめですね、もう一回やり直しましょう。
examplePolite.english: That's no good. Let's do it over.

items.notes: -naosu after a verb stem means 'redo': kakinaosu (rewrite), minaosu (look again).

items.use: Missing something you meant to see, or letting someone off.

example.ja: 昨日のドラマ、見逃した。
example.english: I missed last night's episode.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou no dorama o minogashimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日のドラマを見逃しました。
examplePolite.english: I missed last night's episode.

items.notes: kondo dake minogashite: 'let it slide just this once'.

blocks.label: Luck and doing well
blocks.rationale: Lets you say something's good, you're lucky, it's selling, you guessed right, or someone's thriving.
blocks.interference: ateru (guess right) vs ataru (it hits, you win), and ureru (it sells) vs uru (sell it).

items.use: Casual 'it's fine' or 'it's good': mada ikeru (I can keep going), kore ikeru (this is tasty).

example.ja: これ、結構いけるね！
example.english: This is pretty good!

examplePolite.romaji: kore, kekkou ikemasu ne!
examplePolite.ja: これ、結構いけますね！
examplePolite.english: This is pretty good!

items.notes: Also just 'can go': ashita ikeru? (can you make it tomorrow?). Don't confuse with ikenai (mustn't).

items.use: Mostly as an exclamation, tsuiteru! (lucky!), or in the negative, tsuitenai (no luck).

example.romaji: kyou wa honto ni tsuitenai na.
example.ja: 今日はほんとについてないな。
example.english: I've had no luck at all today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa hontou ni tsuite imasen ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は本当についていませんね。
examplePolite.english: I've had no luck at all today.

items.notes: Same verb as tsuku (stick to), so it can also mean 'it's attached' or 'it's switched on'.

items.use: The goods are the subject: yoku ureru (sells well); also an entertainer making it big.

example.romaji: kono hon, sugoku ureteru rashii yo.
example.ja: この本、すごく売れてるらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently this book is selling really well.

examplePolite.romaji: kono hon wa sugoku urete iru sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: この本はすごく売れているそうです。
examplePolite.english: Apparently this book is selling really well.

items.notes: uru is 'sell' (you sell it); ureru is 'it sells'.

items.use: Guessing an answer, winning a prize, or hitting a target.

example.romaji: nani ga haitteru ka, atete mite.
example.ja: 何が入ってるか、当ててみて。
example.english: Guess what's inside.

examplePolite.romaji: nani ga haitte iru ka, atete mite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 何が入っているか、当ててみてください。
examplePolite.english: Have a guess what's inside.

items.notes: ataru is 'it hits' or 'you win': kuji ga atatta (I won the draw). Also 'put against': te o ateru (put a hand on it).

items.english: do well; play an active part
items.use: Someone shining in their role: at work, on a team, in their field.

example.romaji: kare, ima amerika de katsuyaku shiteru n da tte.
example.ja: 彼、今アメリカで活躍してるんだって。
example.english: I hear he's doing really well in America now.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa ima amerika de katsuyaku shite iru sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は今アメリカで活躍しているそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear he's doing really well in America now.

items.notes: Said of people, not plans; for a plan working out, use umaku iku.

blocks.label: Learning and practice
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about lessons, practice, focus and working out numbers.
blocks.interference: narau needs a teacher, manabu is learning in general, and benkyou suru is studying.

items.use: Repeating something to get better: sport, music, speaking.

example.romaji: shiai no mae ni motto renshuu shiyou.
example.ja: 試合の前にもっと練習しよう。
example.english: Let's practise more before the match.

examplePolite.romaji: shiai no mae ni motto renshuu shimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 試合の前にもっと練習しましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's practise more before the match.

items.notes: Also a noun: renshuu ni iku (go to practice).

items.use: Usually X ni shuuchuu suru (focus on X), or shuuchuu dekinai (can't focus).

example.ja: ここ、うるさくて集中できない。
example.english: It's too noisy here to focus.

examplePolite.romaji: koko wa urusakute shuuchuu dekimasen.
examplePolite.ja: ここはうるさくて集中できません。
examplePolite.english: It's too noisy here to focus.

items.notes: shuuchuuryoku: concentration, attention span.

items.use: Learning from a teacher or in lessons: piano o narau.

example.ja: 子供のころ、ピアノ習ってた。
example.english: I took piano lessons as a kid.

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo no koro, piano o naratte imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 子供のころ、ピアノを習っていました。
examplePolite.english: I took piano lessons as a child.

items.notes: For studying on your own, say benkyou suru.

items.use: Learning in a broad or serious sense, from experience, history or mistakes.

example.romaji: kono shigoto de iroiro mananda yo.
example.ja: この仕事でいろいろ学んだよ。
example.english: I learned a lot from this job.

examplePolite.romaji: kono shigoto de iroiro manabimashita.
examplePolite.ja: この仕事でいろいろ学びました。
examplePolite.english: I learned a lot from this job.

items.notes: narau needs a teacher; manabu doesn't.

items.use: Working out numbers: a bill, costs, time.

example.ja: 一人いくらか計算して。
example.english: Work out how much it is each.

examplePolite.romaji: hitori ikura ka keisan shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 一人いくらか計算してください。
examplePolite.english: Please work out how much it is per person.

items.notes: keisan doori: exactly as planned. keisan ga hayai: quick with numbers.

blocks.label: Lies and getting caught
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about tricking, stealing, covering up and getting caught.
blocks.interference: tsukamaru (get caught) vs tsukamaeru (catch someone).

items.use: Informal; a secret, lie or trick coming out.

example.ja: やばい、彼女にバレた。
example.english: Uh oh, my girlfriend found out.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo ni barete shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女にバレてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: My girlfriend found out.

items.notes: The person who finds out takes ni: oya ni bareta (my parents found out).

items.use: Fooling someone, from a prank to fraud; the passive damasareta (I got tricked) is very common.

example.romaji: damasareta! zenbu uso datta n da.
example.ja: だまされた！全部うそだったんだ。
example.english: I got tricked! It was all lies.

examplePolite.romaji: damasaremashita. zenbu uso datta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: だまされました。全部うそだったんです。
examplePolite.english: I was tricked. It was all lies.

items.notes: Telling a lie is uso o tsuku.

items.english: get caught; get arrested; hold on to
items.use: Being caught by the police or someone chasing you; also grabbing hold: tsurikawa ni tsukamaru (hold the strap).

example.ja: 犯人、やっと捕まったって。
example.english: I heard they finally caught the guy who did it.

examplePolite.romaji: hannin ga yatto tsukamatta sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 犯人がやっと捕まったそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear the culprit has finally been caught.

items.notes: tsukamaeru is 'catch' (someone catches you). Also 'reach someone': kare ni tsukamaranai (I can't get hold of him).

items.use: For 'had X stolen', use the passive: X o nusumareta.

example.ja: 電車で財布盗まれた！
example.english: Someone stole my wallet on the train!

examplePolite.romaji: densha de saifu o nusumaremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 電車で財布を盗まれました。
examplePolite.english: My wallet was stolen on the train.

items.notes: A thief is dorobou.

items.use: Dodging the truth by laughing it off, changing the subject or fudging the numbers.

example.ja: ごまかさないで、ちゃんと答えて。
example.english: Don't dodge it, give me a straight answer.

examplePolite.romaji: gomakasanai de, chanto kotaete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: ごまかさないで、ちゃんと答えてください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't dodge it, give me a straight answer.

items.notes: warai de gomakasu: laugh it off. Milder than damasu.

blocks.label: Born and growing up
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about having a baby, where you grew up and how someone has grown.
blocks.interference: umu (give birth) vs umareru (be born), and sodatsu (grow up) vs sodateru (raise).

items.use: The mother is the subject: kodomo o umu (have a child).

example.romaji: ane ga onna no ko o unda n da.
example.ja: 姉が女の子を産んだんだ。
example.english: My sister had a baby girl.

examplePolite.romaji: ane ga onna no ko o umimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 姉が女の子を産みました。
examplePolite.english: My sister had a baby girl.

items.notes: 'Be born' is umareru: Tokyo de umareta (I was born in Tokyo).

items.use: Where or how someone grew up; also plants and animals growing.

example.romaji: kono machi de sodatta n da.
example.ja: この町で育ったんだ。
example.english: I grew up in this town.

examplePolite.romaji: kono machi de sodachimashita.
examplePolite.ja: この町で育ちました。
examplePolite.english: I grew up in this town.

items.notes: To raise a child is sodateru: kodomo o sodateru.

items.use: Growing up or developing: a child, a person who has matured, a company.

example.ja: 彼、すごく成長したね。
example.english: He's really grown up.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa sugoku seichou shimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼はすごく成長しましたね。
examplePolite.english: He's really grown up.

items.notes: More about growing as a person than sodatsu. Also a noun: seichou ga tanoshimi (can't wait to see you grow).

blocks.label: Girls boys men women
blocks.rationale: Lets you point out and describe the people around you.
blocks.interference: ko (child) vs hito (person); onna no ko can still mean a young woman.

items.use: Also used casually for young women, not just children.

example.ja: あの女の子、誰？
example.english: Who's that girl?

examplePolite.romaji: ano onna no ko wa dare desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: あの女の子は誰ですか？
examplePolite.english: Who is that girl?

items.use: Also used casually for young men.

example.romaji: akachan, otoko no ko datta n da.
example.ja: 赤ちゃん、男の子だったんだ。
example.english: Oh, the baby was a boy!

examplePolite.romaji: akachan wa otoko no ko datta n desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 赤ちゃんは男の子だったんですね。
examplePolite.english: So the baby was a boy.

items.use: The everyday neutral word; dansei is more formal, otoko can sound blunt.

example.romaji: sakki, shiranai otoko no hito ga kita yo.
example.ja: さっき、知らない男の人が来たよ。
example.english: Some man I didn't know came by earlier.

examplePolite.romaji: sakki, shiranai otoko no hito ga kimashita.
examplePolite.ja: さっき、知らない男の人が来ました。
examplePolite.english: A man I didn't know came by earlier.

items.use: The everyday neutral word; josei is more formal, onna can sound blunt.

example.ja: あの女の人、知ってる？
example.english: Do you know that woman?

examplePolite.romaji: ano onna no hito o shitte imasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: あの女の人を知っていますか？
examplePolite.english: Do you know that woman?

blocks.label: Friends and rivals
blocks.rationale: Lets you say who is close to you or on your side.
blocks.interference: yuujin is the formal tomodachi; mikata also means 'way of seeing'.

items.use: Most often in X no mikata (on X's side).

example.romaji: watashi wa zutto mikata da kara ne.
example.ja: 私はずっと味方だからね。
example.english: I'll always be on your side.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi wa zutto mikata desu kara.
examplePolite.ja: 私はずっと味方ですから。
examplePolite.english: I'll always be on your side.

items.notes: Opposite: teki (enemy). Mix-up: mikata also means 'way of seeing' (見方).

items.use: The formal word for friend, used in introductions and speeches; in chat say tomodachi.

example.romaji: kochira wa daigaku jidai no yuujin desu.
example.ja: こちらは大学時代の友人です。
example.english: This is a friend from my university days.

items.use: A really close friend; you can have more than one.

example.romaji: kanojo wa shougakkou kara no shin'yuu na n da.
example.ja: 彼女は小学校からの親友なんだ。
example.english: She's been my best friend since elementary school.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo wa shougakkou kara no shin'yuu desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女は小学校からの親友です。
examplePolite.english: She's been my best friend since elementary school.

example.romaji: ano futari, mukashi kara raibaru na n da.
example.ja: あの二人、昔からライバルなんだ。
example.english: Those two have been rivals forever.

examplePolite.romaji: ano futari wa mukashi kara raibaru desu.
examplePolite.ja: あの二人は昔からライバルです。
examplePolite.english: Those two have been rivals for a long time.

items.notes: Also for love rivals: koi no raibaru.

blocks.label: Moments and nowadays
blocks.rationale: Lets you place things in time: for a second, right about now, earlier, these days.
blocks.interference: Sakihodo (polite 'earlier') vs saki ni (first, ahead).

items.english: a moment; an instant; for a second
items.use: Often alone as an adverb: isshun (for a second), isshun de (in a flash).

example.ja: 一瞬、誰かわからなかった
example.english: For a second, I didn't recognize you.

examplePolite.romaji: isshun, donata ka wakarimasen deshita
examplePolite.ja: 一瞬、どなたかわかりませんでした
examplePolite.english: For a second, I didn't recognize you.

items.notes: Isshun de owatta = it was over in a flash. To ask someone to wait a moment, say chotto.

items.english: about now; by now; this late
items.use: Guesses what's happening elsewhere right now, or complains that something comes too late.

example.ja: 彼、今頃もう着いてるかな
example.english: I wonder if he's there by now.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa imagoro mou tsuite iru deshou ka
examplePolite.ja: 彼は今頃もう着いているでしょうか
examplePolite.english: I wonder if he's there by now.

items.notes: Imagoro nani itteru no? = Why bring that up now? Mainen imagoro = around this time every year.

items.use: The polite form of sakki, heard from staff, on the phone and at work.

example.ja: 先ほどはありがとうございました
example.english: Thank you for earlier.

items.notes: In casual talk say sakki. Don't mix it up with saki ni (first, ahead).

items.use: Usually carries a judgment: imadoki no wakamono (young people these days), imadoki ~ nante (who still does ~?).

example.romaji: imadoki, genkin shika tsukaenai mise nante aru?
example.ja: 今どき、現金しか使えない店なんてある?
example.english: Are there still cash-only shops these days?

examplePolite.romaji: imadoki, genkin shika tsukaenai mise nante arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今どき、現金しか使えない店なんてありますか?
examplePolite.english: Are there still cash-only shops these days?

items.notes: A neutral 'these days' is saikin.

blocks.label: Life, light, boats, visits
blocks.rationale: Four common words for life, light, travel by boat and going to see someone.
blocks.interference: Tazuneru (visit) sounds the same as tazuneru (ask).

items.use: Life as something that can be lost or saved, not life as in daily living.

example.romaji: kono hito wa watashi no inochi no onjin da yo.
example.ja: この人は私の命の恩人だよ。
example.english: This person saved my life.

examplePolite.romaji: kono kata wa watashi no inochi no onjin desu.
examplePolite.ja: この方は私の命の恩人です。
examplePolite.english: This person saved my life.

items.notes: Daily life is seikatsu; your life story or lifetime is jinsei.

items.use: Light you can see, like sunlight or a glow; also hope, figuratively.

example.romaji: mado kara hikari ga haitte kuru ne.
example.ja: 窓から光が入ってくるね。
example.english: Nice light comes in through the window.

examplePolite.romaji: mado kara hikari ga haitte kimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 窓から光が入ってきますね。
examplePolite.english: Nice light comes in through the window.

items.notes: A light you switch on is denki or akari, not hikari. The verb is hikaru (to shine).

items.use: Going to see someone or somewhere on purpose; a bit more formal than ... ni iku.

example.romaji: kinou, mukashi no sensei o tazuneta n da.
example.ja: 昨日、昔の先生を訪ねたんだ。
example.english: Yesterday I went to see my old teacher.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou, mukashi no sensei o tazunemashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日、昔の先生を訪ねました。
examplePolite.english: Yesterday I went to see my old teacher.

items.notes: Sounds the same as tazuneru, 'to ask'. In chat people often just say ... ni asobi ni iku.

example.romaji: shima made fune de ikou yo.
example.ja: 島まで船で行こうよ。
example.english: Let's take the boat to the island.

examplePolite.romaji: shima made fune de ikimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 島まで船で行きましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's take the boat to the island.

items.notes: By boat is fune de; to board is fune ni noru. A ferry is feerii, a small boat booto.

blocks.label: Effort and attitude
blocks.rationale: Lets you say someone means it, tries hard, is brave, proud or rude.
blocks.interference: None.

items.use: Checks or insists that someone means it: honki? (are you serious?), honki da yo (I mean it).

example.romaji: honki de kare to kekkon suru tsumori?
example.ja: 本気で彼と結婚するつもり?
example.english: Are you seriously going to marry him?

examplePolite.romaji: honki de kare to kekkon suru tsumori desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 本気で彼と結婚するつもりですか?
examplePolite.english: Are you seriously planning to marry him?

items.notes: Honki de = seriously, with real effort. Honki ni suru = take a joke at face value.

items.use: How someone acts toward others, usually judged: taido ga warui (rude), sono taido nani? (what's with that attitude?).

example.ja: 彼、最近態度が冷たい
example.english: He's been acting cold lately.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa saikin taido ga tsumetai desu
examplePolite.ja: 彼は最近態度が冷たいです
examplePolite.english: He's been acting cold toward me lately.

items.notes: Taido is outward behavior; the feeling inside is kimochi. Taido ga dekai = acting like you own the place.

items.use: Usually yuuki o dasu (work up the courage) or yuuki ga nai (not have the nerve).

example.ja: 勇気出して告白した
example.english: I worked up the courage and told them how I felt.

examplePolite.romaji: yuuki o dashite kokuhaku shimashita
examplePolite.ja: 勇気を出して告白しました
examplePolite.english: I worked up the courage and told them how I felt.

items.notes: Yuuki o morau = be encouraged by someone or something.

items.use: Almost always zenryoku de (with all your might) or zenryoku o tsukusu (give it your all).

example.romaji: saigo made zenryoku de ganbaru yo
example.ja: 最後まで全力で頑張るよ
example.english: I'll give it everything right to the end.

examplePolite.romaji: saigo made zenryoku de ganbarimasu
examplePolite.ja: 最後まで全力で頑張ります
examplePolite.english: I'll give it everything right to the end.

items.notes: Also used jokingly: zenryoku de kotowaru (refuse flat out).

items.use: Self-respect that gets hurt or gets in the way: puraido ga takai (too proud to back down).

example.romaji: kare wa puraido ga takai kara ayamaranai yo
example.ja: 彼はプライドが高いから謝らないよ
example.english: He's too proud to apologize.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa puraido ga takai node ayamaranai to omoimasu
examplePolite.ja: 彼はプライドが高いので謝らないと思います
examplePolite.english: I think he's too proud to apologize.

items.notes: Puraido ga kizutsuku = your pride gets hurt. Being proud of something good is hokori.

blocks.label: Shock and hard times
blocks.rationale: Lets you say something hurt, was awful, or was a hard thing to go through.
blocks.interference: Shokku means hurt and let down, not surprised (bikkuri).

items.use: Emotional hurt or disappointment: shokku! (I'm gutted), shokku o ukeru (be hit hard).

example.romaji: sore kiite, maji de shokku datta
example.ja: それ聞いて、マジでショックだった
example.english: Hearing that really hurt.

examplePolite.romaji: sore o kiite, hontou ni shokku deshita
examplePolite.ja: それを聞いて、本当にショックでした
examplePolite.english: I was really upset to hear that.

items.notes: Mostly 'hurt and let down', not surprise; for surprise say bikkuri.

items.use: Used loosely for any awful situation.

example.romaji: manin densha, maiasa jigoku da yo
example.ja: 満員電車、毎朝地獄だよ
example.english: The packed train is hell every morning.

examplePolite.romaji: manin densha wa maiasa jigoku desu
examplePolite.ja: 満員電車は毎朝地獄です
examplePolite.english: The packed train is hell every morning.

items.notes: Opposite: tengoku (heaven).

items.english: go through (a feeling); have a (hard, lonely...) time
items.use: Always after a feeling word: tsurai omoi o suru (have a hard time), hazukashii omoi o suru (be embarrassed).

example.romaji: kodomo no koro, sabishii omoi o shita
example.ja: 子供の頃、寂しい思いをした
example.english: I was lonely a lot as a kid.

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo no koro, sabishii omoi o shimashita
examplePolite.ja: 子供の頃、寂しい思いをしました
examplePolite.english: I was often lonely as a child.

items.notes: Omoi o saseru = put someone through it: tsurai omoi sasete gomen (sorry for putting you through so much).

blocks.label: Cause and effect
blocks.rationale: Lets you say what caused something and what it led to.
blocks.interference: Gen'in is the cause of a problem; kikkake is what got something started.

items.use: The cause of a problem, illness or accident.

example.romaji: kenka no gen'in wa nan datta no?
example.ja: 喧嘩の原因は何だったの？
example.english: What started the fight?

examplePolite.romaji: kenka no gen'in wa nan deshita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 喧嘩の原因は何でしたか？
examplePolite.english: What caused the argument?

items.notes: Riyuu is a reason someone gives; gen'in is what made something happen.

items.english: what got it started; trigger; chance
items.use: How something began, like a hobby or a relationship; X ga kikkake de = X got it started.

example.romaji: nihongo hajimeta kikkake wa anime da yo.
example.ja: 日本語始めたきっかけはアニメだよ。
example.english: Anime is what got me into Japanese.

examplePolite.romaji: nihongo o hajimeta kikkake wa anime desu.
examplePolite.ja: 日本語を始めたきっかけはアニメです。
examplePolite.english: Anime is what got me into Japanese.

items.notes: Kikkake wa? = What got you into it? is a standard small-talk question.

items.use: Usually 'X no eikyou de' (because of X) or 'eikyou o ukeru' (be influenced).

example.romaji: ani no eikyou de gitaa hajimeta.
example.ja: 兄の影響でギター始めた。
example.english: I took up guitar because of my big brother.

examplePolite.romaji: ani no eikyou de gitaa o hajimemashita.
examplePolite.ja: 兄の影響でギターを始めました。
examplePolite.english: I took up guitar because of my big brother.

items.notes: Also for weather and events: taifuu no eikyou de = because of the typhoon.

items.english: effect; result (of a remedy or effort)
items.use: Kouka ga aru / nai = it works / doesn't work.

example.ja: この薬、全然効果ない。
example.english: This medicine isn't working at all.

examplePolite.romaji: kono kusuri wa zenzen kouka ga arimasen.
examplePolite.ja: この薬は全然効果がありません。
examplePolite.english: This medicine isn't working at all.

items.notes: The verb kiku (work, take effect) is often used instead.

blocks.label: Impressions and behaviour
blocks.rationale: Lets you describe how someone comes across, acts and is treated.
blocks.interference: Imeeji is an impression in your mind, not a photo.

items.use: How you picture or think of something, not a photo; imeeji to chigau = not what I expected.

example.ja: なんかイメージと違うね。
example.english: It's not quite what I pictured.

examplePolite.romaji: nanka imeeji to chigaimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: なんかイメージと違いますね。
examplePolite.english: It's not quite what I pictured.

items.notes: Imeeji suru = picture, imagine; a photo is shashin.

items.use: Sounds a little serious; koudou ni utsusu = put into action.

example.romaji: kare no koudou, chotto okashii yo.
example.ja: 彼の行動、ちょっとおかしいよ。
example.english: He's been acting a bit strange.

examplePolite.romaji: kare no koudou ga chotto okashii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼の行動がちょっとおかしいです。
examplePolite.english: He's been acting a bit strange.

items.notes: Koudou suru = act, take action; for an everyday 'do', just use suru or yaru.

items.use: Mostly how someone is treated: X atsukai suru = treat someone as X.

example.ja: 子ども扱いしないでよ。
example.english: Don't treat me like a child.

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo atsukai shinai de kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 子ども扱いしないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't treat me like a child.

items.notes: The verb is atsukau (handle, treat); atsukai ga hidoi = they treat you badly.

items.use: Casually, nazo alone means 'no idea, it's a mystery' about anything odd.

example.romaji: ano hito, nazo da yo ne.
example.ja: あの人、謎だよね。
example.english: That guy's a real mystery, isn't he?

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito wa nazo desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの人は謎ですね。
examplePolite.english: That person's a real mystery.

items.notes: Nazonazo = a riddle.

items.use: Ii shigeki ni naru = be inspiring, give you a push.

example.romaji: kare to hanasu to ii shigeki ni naru.
example.ja: 彼と話すといい刺激になる。
example.english: Talking to him really fires me up.

examplePolite.romaji: kare to hanasu to ii shigeki ni narimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼と話すといい刺激になります。
examplePolite.english: Talking to him is really inspiring.

items.notes: Shigeki ga tsuyoi = too strong or harsh, of spicy food, skin products or a film's content.

blocks.label: Trouble and limits
blocks.rationale: Lets you apologise for trouble and say you've had enough.
blocks.interference: Toraburu is something going wrong; meiwaku is trouble you cause someone.

items.use: Often 'mou genkai' (I can't take any more) when tired, full or fed up.

example.ja: もう限界、ちょっと休もう。
example.english: I can't go on, let's take a break.

examplePolite.romaji: mou genkai desu, chotto yasumimashou.
examplePolite.ja: もう限界です、ちょっと休みましょう。
examplePolite.english: I've hit my limit, let's take a break.

items.use: The polite form of meiwaku, used mostly in set apologies.

example.romaji: gomeiwaku o okake shite, sumimasen deshita.
example.ja: ご迷惑をおかけして、すみませんでした。
example.english: I'm sorry for all the trouble I caused you.

items.notes: Casually it's plain meiwaku: meiwaku kakete gomen (sorry for the bother).

items.use: Something going wrong, like a breakdown, a mix-up or a falling-out.

example.romaji: shigoto de chotto toraburu ga atte.
example.ja: 仕事でちょっとトラブルがあって。
example.english: There was a bit of trouble at work.

examplePolite.romaji: shigoto de chotto toraburu ga arimashite.
examplePolite.ja: 仕事でちょっとトラブルがありまして。
examplePolite.english: There was a bit of trouble at work.

items.notes: For trouble you cause someone, the word is meiwaku; for being in trouble with someone, okorareru (get told off).

items.use: Futan ni naru = become a burden; futan o kakeru = put a burden on someone.

example.romaji: kare ni futan kaketakunai n da.
example.ja: 彼に負担かけたくないんだ。
example.english: I don't want to be a burden on him.

examplePolite.romaji: kare ni futan o kaketakunai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼に負担をかけたくないんです。
examplePolite.english: I don't want to be a burden on him.

items.notes: Futan suru = pay, cover a cost.

blocks.label: Basics and conditions
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk through what something involves and choose between options.
blocks.interference: Jouken means terms, not physical condition.

items.use: Kihon (or kihonteki ni) at the start of a sentence = basically, as a rule.

example.ja: 基本、夜は自炊してる。
example.english: I basically cook for myself in the evenings.

examplePolite.romaji: kihonteki ni, yoru wa jisui shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 基本的に、夜は自炊しています。
examplePolite.english: I basically cook for myself in the evenings.

items.use: For the terms of a deal, a job or a flat; X ga jouken = on condition that X.

example.ja: 一つだけ条件がある。
example.english: I've got one condition.

examplePolite.romaji: hitotsu dake jouken ga arimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 一つだけ条件があります。
examplePolite.english: I have just one condition.

items.notes: Not physical condition; that's choushi or guai.

items.english: content; what it's about; the details
items.use: What's in a film, a talk, a job or a message.

example.ja: その映画、どんな内容？
example.english: What's that film about?

examplePolite.romaji: sono eiga wa donna naiyou desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: その映画はどんな内容ですか？
examplePolite.english: What's that film about?

items.use: Options on a shortlist, like places, names or dates, as well as election candidates.

example.romaji: ryokousaki no kouho, ikutsu ka aru yo.
example.ja: 旅行先の候補、いくつかあるよ。
example.english: I've got a few options for where to go.

examplePolite.romaji: ryokousaki no kouho ga ikutsu ka arimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 旅行先の候補がいくつかあります。
examplePolite.english: I have a few options for where to travel.

items.notes: Daiichi kouho = first choice.

blocks.label: Opinions and excuses
blocks.rationale: Lets you ask for views, give advice and push back on excuses.
blocks.interference: Iken is your view; tachiba is the position you're in.

items.use: Sounds a bit formal; casually people ask dou omou? (what do you think?) instead.

example.ja: みんなの意見聞きたいな。
example.english: I'd like to hear what everyone thinks.

examplePolite.romaji: minasan no iken o kikitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: みなさんの意見を聞きたいです。
examplePolite.english: I'd like to hear everyone's opinion.

items.use: Often 'X no tachiba ni naru' (put yourself in X's shoes).

example.romaji: ore no tachiba mo kangaete yo.
example.ja: 俺の立場も考えてよ。
example.english: Think about my position too.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi no tachiba mo kangaete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 私の立場も考えてください。
examplePolite.english: Please think about my position too.

items.notes: About your role and circumstances, not a physical position (ichi).

items.use: Iiwake suru = make excuses.

example.ja: 言い訳しないでよ。
example.english: Don't make excuses.

examplePolite.romaji: iiwake wa shinai de kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 言い訳はしないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't make excuses.

items.notes: Iiwake ja nai kedo... = I'm not making excuses, but...

items.use: Adobaisu suru = give advice; adobaisu o morau = get advice.

example.ja: なんかいいアドバイスある？
example.english: Got any good advice?

examplePolite.romaji: nanika ii adobaisu wa arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 何かいいアドバイスはありますか？
examplePolite.english: Do you have any good advice?

items.notes: More common in speech than the formal word jogen.

blocks.label: Replies and reactions
blocks.rationale: Lets you say whether someone answered and how they reacted.
blocks.interference: Henji is any reply; henshin is only a reply to a message.

items.use: Any reply, spoken or written, including answering when your name is called; often 'henji suru'.

example.romaji: yonde mo henji shinai n da yo.
example.ja: 呼んでも返事しないんだよ。
example.english: He doesn't answer even when I call him.

examplePolite.romaji: yonde mo henji o shinai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 呼んでも返事をしないんです。
examplePolite.english: He doesn't answer even when I call him.

items.notes: For texts and emails, henshin is more specific.

items.use: Usually 'henshin suru' or 'henshin ga kuru' (get a reply).

example.ja: 彼女からまだ返信来ない。
example.english: She still hasn't replied.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo kara mada henshin ga kimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女からまだ返信が来ません。
examplePolite.english: She still hasn't replied.

items.notes: Same sound as henshin 'transformation', as in superheroes.

items.use: How someone reacts to news, a joke or a message; hannou ga nai = no response.

example.ja: 彼の反応、どうだった？
example.english: How did he react?

examplePolite.romaji: kare no hannou wa dou deshita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 彼の反応はどうでしたか？
examplePolite.english: How did he react?

items.notes: Hannou suru = react.

blocks.label: Home and neighbours
blocks.rationale: Lets you say where you live and refer politely to other people's homes.
blocks.interference: Manshon is any apartment block, not a mansion; otaku (your home) sounds like otaku (geek).

items.use: The area right around your home; kinjo no = local, nearby.

example.romaji: kinjo ni oishii pan'ya aru yo.
example.ja: 近所においしいパン屋あるよ。
example.english: There's a good bakery near me.

examplePolite.romaji: kinjo ni oishii pan'ya ga arimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 近所においしいパン屋がありますよ。
examplePolite.english: There's a good bakery near me.

items.notes: Kinjo no hito = the neighbours; tonari is the house right next door.

items.use: Any solid, multi-storey block of flats or a flat in one, not a mansion.

example.romaji: eki no chikaku no manshon ni sunderu.
example.ja: 駅の近くのマンションに住んでる。
example.english: I live in an apartment near the station.

examplePolite.romaji: eki no chikaku no manshon ni sunde imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 駅の近くのマンションに住んでいます。
examplePolite.english: I live in an apartment near the station.

items.notes: Apaato is a cheaper, usually low-rise wooden building.

items.use: A slightly formal word heard at work, in news and on forms.

example.romaji: kyou wa jitaku de shigoto shiteru.
example.ja: 今日は自宅で仕事してる。
example.english: I'm working from home today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa jitaku de shigoto o shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は自宅で仕事をしています。
examplePolite.english: I'm working from home today.

items.notes: Uchi and ie are the everyday words for home.

items.use: A polite way to refer to another person's house or family.

example.romaji: ashita, otaku ni ukagatte mo ii desu ka?
example.ja: 明日、お宅に伺ってもいいですか？
example.english: May I come round to your home tomorrow?

items.notes: Written オタク, the same sound means a geek or obsessive fan.

blocks.label: School stages
blocks.rationale: Lets you place memories by school stage, from primary to high school.
blocks.interference: Chuugaku is middle school and koukou is high school; they're easy to swap.

items.use: Short for koutou gakkou; covers about ages 15 to 18.

example.ja: 高校の時、野球やってた。
example.english: I played baseball in high school.

examplePolite.romaji: koukou no toki, yakyuu o yatte imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 高校の時、野球をやっていました。
examplePolite.english: I played baseball in high school.

items.notes: Koukousei = a high-school student.

items.use: Six years, about ages 6 to 12.

example.romaji: shougakkou kara no tomodachi na n da.
example.ja: 小学校からの友達なんだ。
example.english: We've been friends since elementary school.

examplePolite.romaji: shougakkou kara no tomodachi na n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 小学校からの友達なんです。
examplePolite.english: We've been friends since elementary school.

items.notes: Shougakusei = an elementary-school pupil.

items.use: Short for chuugakkou; about ages 12 to 15.

example.ja: 中学の時、テニス部だった。
example.english: I was in the tennis club in middle school.

examplePolite.romaji: chuugaku no toki wa tenisubu deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 中学の時はテニス部でした。
examplePolite.english: I was in the tennis club in middle school.

items.notes: Chuugakusei = a middle-school student.

items.english: classroom; class, lessons (for a hobby or skill)

example.ja: 教室に忘れ物しちゃった。
example.english: I left something in the classroom.

examplePolite.romaji: kyoushitsu ni wasuremono o shite shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 教室に忘れ物をしてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I left something in the classroom.

items.notes: Adults hear the second sense most: ryouri kyoushitsu (cooking class), eikaiwa kyoushitsu (English school).

blocks.label: Shops and parks
blocks.rationale: Lets you say where you're popping out to nearby.
blocks.interference: Omise covers restaurants and bars too, not just shops.

items.use: The everyday, slightly polite word for any shop or place to eat; plain mise sounds rougher.

example.ja: このお店、すごくおいしいよ。
example.english: This place is really good.

examplePolite.romaji: kono omise, sugoku oishii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: このお店、すごくおいしいですよ。
examplePolite.english: This place is really good.

items.notes: Often means a restaurant or bar, not just a shop.

items.use: Short for konbiniensu sutoa; nobody says the long form.

example.ja: ちょっとコンビニ行ってくるね。
example.english: I'm just popping to the convenience store.

examplePolite.romaji: chotto konbini ni itte kimasu.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっとコンビニに行ってきます。
examplePolite.english: I'll just pop to the convenience store.

items.use: Short for suupaa maaketto; said alone it always means the shop.

example.ja: 帰りにスーパー寄る？
example.english: Shall we stop at the supermarket on the way home?

examplePolite.romaji: kaeri ni suupaa ni yorimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 帰りにスーパーに寄りますか？
examplePolite.english: Shall we stop at the supermarket on the way home?

items.notes: Not 'super' as in great; that's sugoi or saikou.

example.ja: 公園で少し歩く？
example.english: Want to walk in the park for a bit?

examplePolite.romaji: kouen de sukoshi arukimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 公園で少し歩きませんか？
examplePolite.english: Shall we walk in the park for a bit?

items.notes: Same sound as kouen (a talk or a show); context makes it clear.

blocks.label: Gifts and letters
blocks.rationale: Lets you give a present, return the favour and write to someone.
blocks.interference: Okaeshi is also what shop staff say when handing over change.

example.ja: 誕生日プレゼント、何がいい?
example.english: What do you want for your birthday?

examplePolite.romaji: tanjoubi purezento wa nani ga ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 誕生日プレゼントは何がいいですか?
examplePolite.english: What would you like for your birthday?

items.notes: Also a verb: purezento suru = give as a gift. Souvenirs from a trip are omiyage.

items.english: something in return; return gift; payback
items.use: Mostly the gift you give back after receiving one, as custom expects.

example.ja: これ、この間のお返し。
example.english: This is to thank you for the other day.

examplePolite.romaji: kore, kono aida no okaeshi desu.
examplePolite.ja: これ、この間のお返しです。
examplePolite.english: This is to thank you for the other day.

items.notes: Shop staff say it for your change: hyaku en no okaeshi desu. Okaeshi da! can also mean 'Take that!'

example.ja: おばあちゃんに手紙書いたよ。
example.english: I wrote Grandma a letter.

examplePolite.romaji: sobo ni tegami o kakimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 祖母に手紙を書きました。
examplePolite.english: I wrote my grandmother a letter.

items.notes: Send one = dasu; a postcard is a hagaki.

blocks.label: Meals and food
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about meals and ask about food and drink.
blocks.interference: Gohan, shokuji and meshi all mean meal; gohan is the default, shokuji more formal, meshi rough.

items.use: The everyday word for any meal: asagohan, hirugohan and bangohan are breakfast, lunch and dinner.

example.romaji: issho ni gohan tabe ni ikou yo
example.ja: 一緒にご飯食べに行こうよ
example.english: Let's go get something to eat together.

examplePolite.romaji: issho ni gohan tabe ni ikimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 一緒にご飯食べに行きませんか?
examplePolite.english: Would you like to go and eat together?

items.notes: Also plain cooked rice: gohan o taku means cook the rice.

items.use: A step more formal than gohan; common in invitations, at restaurants and in health talk.

example.ja: 今度食事でもどう?
example.english: How about dinner sometime?

examplePolite.romaji: kondo oshokuji demo ikaga desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今度お食事でもいかがですか?
examplePolite.english: Would you like to have dinner sometime?

items.notes: Shokuji suru means to have a meal. Oshokuji is the polite form for someone else's meal.

items.use: Rough word for gohan, used mostly by men among friends.

example.ja: 腹減った、飯行こうぜ
example.english: I'm starving, let's go eat.

items.notes: Also heard in hirumeshi (lunch) and yorumeshi (dinner). Say gohan yourself unless you're among close friends.

items.use: Used for kinds of food, as in favourite foods or foods you can't eat.

example.ja: 好きな食べ物は何?
example.english: What's your favourite food?

examplePolite.romaji: suki na tabemono wa nan desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 好きな食べ物は何ですか?
examplePolite.english: What's your favourite food?

items.notes: Pairs with nomimono (drink).

example.ja: 飲み物は何にする?
example.english: What do you want to drink?

examplePolite.romaji: nomimono wa nani ni shimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 飲み物は何にしますか?
examplePolite.english: What would you like to drink?

items.notes: Staff say onomimono: 'onomimono wa?' asks for your drink order.

blocks.label: Office tasks
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about everyday office work.
blocks.interference: Shiryou are the prepared papers; deeta is the raw numbers or files.

items.use: Papers or files prepared for a meeting or research, printed or digital.

example.ja: 会議の資料もう送った?
example.english: Did you send the meeting materials yet?

examplePolite.romaji: kaigi no shiryou wa mou okurimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 会議の資料はもう送りましたか?
examplePolite.english: Have you sent the meeting documents yet?

items.notes: Shiryou o tsukuru means prepare the documents.

items.use: A talk you give in class or at work, or results being announced.

example.romaji: ashita happyou aru kara kinchou suru
example.ja: 明日発表あるから緊張する
example.english: I've got a presentation tomorrow, I'm nervous.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita happyou ga aru node kinchou shite imasu
examplePolite.ja: 明日発表があるので緊張しています
examplePolite.english: I have a presentation tomorrow, so I'm nervous.

items.notes: Happyou suru means present or announce. Kekka happyou is the announcement of results.

items.use: What a boss or leader tells you to do.

example.romaji: ue no shiji o matteru toko
example.ja: 上の指示を待ってるとこ
example.english: I'm waiting for instructions from above.

examplePolite.romaji: ue no shiji o matte iru tokoro desu
examplePolite.ja: 上の指示を待っているところです
examplePolite.english: I'm waiting for instructions from my superiors.

items.notes: Shiji o dasu means give instructions. Shiji also sounds like the word for support.

items.use: Also means digital files in general, like photos and documents.

example.ja: パソコンのデータ全部消えちゃった
example.english: Everything on my computer got wiped.

examplePolite.romaji: pasokon no deeta ga zenbu kiete shimaimashita
examplePolite.ja: パソコンのデータが全部消えてしまいました
examplePolite.english: All the data on my computer was lost.

blocks.label: School life
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about your class, club, graduating and qualifications.
blocks.interference: Kurasu is your class group; a single lesson is jugyou.

items.use: The group you're in at school, not a single lesson; a lesson is jugyou.

example.ja: 同じクラスだったよね?
example.english: We were in the same class, right?

examplePolite.romaji: onaji kurasu deshita yo ne?
examplePolite.ja: 同じクラスでしたよね?
examplePolite.english: We were in the same class, weren't we?

items.notes: Also a level or grade, as in hai kurasu (high-end).

items.use: Used for finishing any level of school, not just university.

example.romaji: rainen daigaku sotsugyou suru n da
example.ja: 来年大学卒業するんだ
example.english: I graduate from university next year.

examplePolite.romaji: rainen daigaku o sotsugyou shimasu
examplePolite.ja: 来年大学を卒業します
examplePolite.english: I'll graduate from university next year.

items.notes: Takes o: daigaku o sotsugyou suru. Also used for leaving a group or growing out of a habit. Sotsugyoushiki is the graduation ceremony.

items.use: Mostly a school sports or hobby club, named by its activity, like sakkaabu (soccer club).

example.romaji: bu no renshuu ga mainichi aru n da
example.ja: 部の練習が毎日あるんだ
example.english: We have club practice every day.

examplePolite.romaji: bu no renshuu ga mainichi aru n desu
examplePolite.ja: 部の練習が毎日あるんです
examplePolite.english: We have club practice every day.

items.notes: Bukatsu is club activities. In a company it means a department, like eigyoubu (sales).

items.english: qualification; licence; the right (to do something)

example.romaji: shigoto no tame ni shikaku torou to omotte
example.ja: 仕事のために資格取ろうと思って
example.english: I'm thinking of getting a qualification for work.

examplePolite.romaji: shigoto no tame ni shikaku o torou to omotte imasu
examplePolite.ja: 仕事のために資格を取ろうと思っています
examplePolite.english: I'm planning to get a qualification for my job.

items.notes: Shikaku o toru means get a qualification. Iu shikaku nai means you have no right to say that.

blocks.label: Teams and workplaces
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about where you work and who you work with.
blocks.interference: Shokuba is any workplace, jimusho an office or agency, genba where the hands-on work happens.

example.ja: 同じチームで頑張ろう
example.english: We're on the same team, let's give it our all.

examplePolite.romaji: onaji chiimu de ganbarimashou
examplePolite.ja: 同じチームで頑張りましょう
examplePolite.english: Let's do our best together on the same team.

items.use: Where the hands-on work happens, like a building site, film set or shop floor.

example.ja: 今から現場行ってくる
example.english: I'm heading out to the site now.

examplePolite.romaji: ima kara genba ni itte kimasu
examplePolite.ja: 今から現場に行ってきます
examplePolite.english: I'm going out to the site now.

items.notes: In crime dramas it's the crime or accident scene.

items.use: Someone paid or highly skilled; puro mitai is praise: like a pro.

example.romaji: sasuga puro da ne, zenzen chigau
example.ja: さすがプロだね、全然違う
example.english: That's a pro for you, it's on another level.

examplePolite.romaji: sasuga puro desu ne, zenzen chigaimasu
examplePolite.ja: さすがプロですね、全然違います
examplePolite.english: As expected of a pro, it's completely different.

items.notes: The opposite is shirouto (amateur).

items.use: A small business's office or an agency's base; a big company's office is usually just kaisha.

example.ja: 一回事務所に戻るね
example.english: I'm heading back to the office for a bit.

examplePolite.romaji: ichido jimusho ni modorimasu
examplePolite.ja: 一度事務所に戻ります
examplePolite.english: I'll head back to the office for a bit.

items.notes: Geinou jimusho is a talent agency, as heard in celebrity news.

items.use: Where you work and the people there, whatever the job.

example.romaji: shokuba no hito to wa anmari nomanai
example.ja: 職場の人とはあんまり飲まない
example.english: I don't really go drinking with people from work.

examplePolite.romaji: shokuba no hito to wa amari nomimasen
examplePolite.ja: 職場の人とはあまり飲みません
examplePolite.english: I don't drink much with my coworkers.

blocks.label: Feeling unwell
blocks.rationale: Say you're not feeling well and why.
blocks.interference: Choushi and guai both mean 'condition'; guai leans toward feeling physically ill.

items.use: For how you, your body, a machine or things in general are doing; choushi dou? = how's it going?

example.ja: 久しぶり！最近、調子どう？
example.english: Long time no see! How've you been?

examplePolite.romaji: ohisashiburi desu. saikin, choushi wa dou desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: お久しぶりです。最近、調子はどうですか？
examplePolite.english: It's been a while. How have you been?

items.notes: Choushi ga warui = not feeling well, or not working right. Choushi ni noru = get carried away.

items.use: Usually means a fever: netsu ga aru = have a temperature.

example.romaji: chotto netsu aru kara, kyou wa yasumu ne.
example.ja: ちょっと熱あるから、今日は休むね。
example.english: I've got a bit of a fever, so I'm taking today off.

examplePolite.romaji: sukoshi netsu ga aru node, kyou wa yasumimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 少し熱があるので、今日は休みます。
examplePolite.english: I have a slight fever, so I'll take today off.

items.notes: Netsu o hakaru = take your temperature; netsu ga sagatta = the fever's gone down.

items.use: You 'pull' a cold: kaze o hiku; kaze hiita = I've caught a cold.

example.romaji: kaze hiita mitai, nodo ga itai.
example.ja: 風邪ひいたみたい、喉が痛い。
example.english: I think I've caught a cold; my throat hurts.

examplePolite.romaji: kaze o hiita mitai de, nodo ga itai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 風邪をひいたみたいで、喉が痛いです。
examplePolite.english: I think I've caught a cold, and my throat hurts.

items.notes: Same sound as kaze (wind); context tells them apart. Kazegusuri = cold medicine.

items.english: how you feel (health); condition; how something works
items.use: Mostly asked about health: guai ga warui = feel sick.

example.ja: 大丈夫？具合悪いの？
example.english: Are you okay? Not feeling well?

examplePolite.romaji: daijoubu desu ka? guai ga warui n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 大丈夫ですか？具合が悪いんですか？
examplePolite.english: Are you all right? Are you feeling unwell?

items.notes: Close to choushi, but guai leans toward feeling physically ill. Konna guai ni = like this, this way.

items.english: lack of sleep; not getting enough sleep
items.use: Often given as the reason you're off: nebusoku de = because I didn't sleep enough.

example.ja: 寝不足で頭が回らない。
example.english: I'm so short on sleep I can't think straight.

examplePolite.romaji: nebusoku de, atama ga mawaranai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 寝不足で、頭が回らないんです。
examplePolite.english: I haven't slept enough, so I can't think straight.

blocks.label: Society and the news
blocks.rationale: Comment on the news and how the world works.
blocks.interference: Jiken (incident, crime) gets mixed up with jiko (accident); yo no naka and shakai overlap.

items.use: A crime or shocking event, as in the news or detective shows; jokingly, any big deal.

example.romaji: kinjo de jiken ga atta rashii yo.
example.ja: 近所で事件があったらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently something happened in the neighbourhood.

examplePolite.romaji: kinjo de jiken ga atta rashii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 近所で事件があったらしいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Apparently there was an incident in the neighbourhood.

items.notes: Jiko is an accident; jiken is something people did, often a crime.

items.use: Used when commenting on how the world or life works.

example.romaji: yo no naka, sonna ni amaku nai yo.
example.ja: 世の中、そんなに甘くないよ。
example.english: Life isn't that easy, you know.

examplePolite.romaji: yo no naka wa sonna ni amaku nai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 世の中はそんなに甘くないですよ。
examplePolite.english: The world isn't that easy, you know.

items.notes: Shakai is society as a system; yo no naka is the world as people live it.

items.use: Society in general, and especially adult working life after school.

example.ja: 社会に出れば分かるよ。
example.english: You'll get it once you're out in the real world.

examplePolite.romaji: shakai ni dereba wakarimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 社会に出れば分かりますよ。
examplePolite.english: You'll understand once you start working.

items.notes: Shakaijin = a working adult. At school, shakai is social studies.

items.use: News media and reporters, often said with a critical tone.

example.romaji: masukomi tte, sugu oogesa ni iu yo ne.
example.ja: マスコミって、すぐ大げさに言うよね。
example.english: The media always blow things out of proportion, don't they?

examplePolite.romaji: masukomi wa sugu oogesa ni iimasu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: マスコミはすぐ大げさに言いますよね。
examplePolite.english: The media do tend to exaggerate, don't they?

items.notes: From 'mass communication'. Media is also used and sounds more neutral.

blocks.label: Rules and permission
blocks.rationale: Say what's allowed, what's banned and what's your right.
blocks.interference: None.

items.use: Formal or official permission; kyoka o morau = get permission.

example.ja: それ、上司の許可もらった？
example.english: Did you get your boss's okay for that?

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa joushi no kyoka o moraimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: それは上司の許可をもらいましたか？
examplePolite.english: Did you get your manager's approval for that?

items.notes: Kyoka suru = to permit. Day to day, people just ask ii? to ask if something's okay.

items.use: Rules of a game, a house or a group; mamoru = follow them, yaburu = break them.

example.ja: ルールはちゃんと守ってよ。
example.english: Stick to the rules, okay?

examplePolite.romaji: ruuru wa chanto mamotte kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: ルールはちゃんと守ってくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Please make sure you follow the rules.

items.notes: Kisoku is the more formal word for regulations, like school rules.

items.use: Said of rules (X wa kinshi = X isn't allowed) and ends many signs.

example.ja: ここ、タバコ禁止だよ。
example.english: You can't smoke here.

examplePolite.romaji: koko wa tabako kinshi desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: ここはタバコ禁止ですよ。
examplePolite.english: Smoking isn't allowed here.

items.notes: On signs: chuusha kinshi = no parking; satsuei kinshi = no photos.

items.use: Often in arguments: ... kenri wa nai = you have no right to ...

example.romaji: anata ni sonna koto o iu kenri wa nai.
example.ja: あなたにそんなことを言う権利はない。
example.english: You have no right to say that.

examplePolite.romaji: anata ni sonna koto o iu kenri wa arimasen.
examplePolite.ja: あなたにそんなことを言う権利はありません。
examplePolite.english: You have no right to say that.

items.notes: Kenri ga aru = have the right. Its pair is gimu (duty).

blocks.label: Dates and nights out
blocks.rationale: Make plans for dates, drinks and parties.
blocks.interference: A paatii is a planned party; drinks with coworkers is a nomikai.

example.romaji: shuumatsu, kanojo to deeto suru n da.
example.ja: 週末、彼女とデートするんだ。
example.english: I've got a date with my girlfriend this weekend.

examplePolite.romaji: shuumatsu, kanojo to deeto suru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 週末、彼女とデートするんです。
examplePolite.english: I've got a date with my girlfriend this weekend.

items.notes: Used as deeto suru or deeto ni iku. Never a calendar date; that's hizuke.

items.use: A group drinking session with coworkers, classmates or friends, usually at an izakaya.

example.romaji: kyou nomikai da kara, bangohan iranai.
example.ja: 今日飲み会だから、晩ご飯いらない。
example.english: I'm out drinking tonight, so I don't need dinner.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa nomikai ga aru node, bangohan wa irimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は飲み会があるので、晩ご飯はいりません。
examplePolite.english: I have a drinking party tonight, so I won't need dinner.

items.notes: The second round somewhere else is the nijikai.

items.use: A planned party; drinks with friends or coworkers is usually a nomikai.

example.romaji: kin'you, tomodachi no ie de paatii aru n da.
example.ja: 金曜、友達の家でパーティーあるんだ。
example.english: There's a party at a friend's place on Friday.

examplePolite.romaji: kin'youbi ni tomodachi no ie de paatii ga aru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 金曜日に友達の家でパーティーがあるんです。
examplePolite.english: There's a party at a friend's place on Friday.

items.notes: Common as tanjoubi paatii (birthday party) and hoomu paatii (party at someone's home).

items.use: A cocktail-style bar; a cheap place for drinks and food is an izakaya.

example.romaji: kono ato, baa de ippai nomanai?
example.ja: この後、バーで一杯飲まない？
example.english: Want to grab a drink at a bar after this?

examplePolite.romaji: kono ato, baa de ippai nomimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: この後、バーで一杯飲みませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like a drink at a bar after this?

blocks.label: Messages and online
blocks.rationale: Talk about emailing, messaging and doing things online.
blocks.interference: Meeru is often any phone message, not only email.

items.use: Older people use it for any phone message; for chat apps younger people say rain (LINE).

example.ja: 後でメールするね。
example.english: I'll email you later.

examplePolite.romaji: ato de meeru shimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 後でメールしますね。
examplePolite.english: I'll email you later.

items.notes: Meeru suru = send one; meeru ga kita = I got one.

items.use: Netto de = online, as in netto de katta (bought it online).

example.ja: それ、ネットで調べてみよう。
example.english: Let's look that up online.

examplePolite.romaji: sore, netto de shirabete mimashou.
examplePolite.ja: それ、ネットで調べてみましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's look that up online.

items.notes: Also a net, as in tennis or fishing.

items.use: Chat messages, voicemail or a written note.

example.ja: メッセージ送ったけど、見た？
example.english: I sent you a message, did you see it?

examplePolite.romaji: messeeji o okurimashita ga, mimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: メッセージを送りましたが、見ましたか？
examplePolite.english: I sent you a message. Did you see it?

items.notes: Goes with okuru (send) and kaesu (reply).

items.use: Short for tsuushin hanbai; now it mostly means buying online.

example.romaji: kore, tsuuhan de katta n da.
example.ja: これ、通販で買ったんだ。
example.english: I bought this online.

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa tsuuhan de katta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: これは通販で買ったんです。
examplePolite.english: I bought this online.

items.notes: Netto de katta (bought it online) means the same.

blocks.label: Hobbies and shows
blocks.rationale: Talk about what you like doing and watching.
blocks.interference: Dorama is a scripted series; bangumi is any show on TV.

items.use: Shumi wa? is the classic getting-to-know-you question.

example.ja: 趣味って何かある？
example.english: Do you have any hobbies?

examplePolite.romaji: shumi wa nan desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 趣味は何ですか？
examplePolite.english: What are your hobbies?

items.notes: Also taste: shumi ga ii (good taste), shumi ja nai (not my thing).

items.use: Any scripted TV series, foreign ones too: kankoku dorama (Korean dramas).

example.ja: 今、なんか面白いドラマある？
example.english: Is there any good drama on right now?

examplePolite.romaji: ima, nanika omoshiroi dorama wa arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今、何か面白いドラマはありますか？
examplePolite.english: Are there any good dramas on right now?

items.use: Any show on a channel: news, variety, quiz; scripted series are dorama.

example.romaji: kono bangumi, maishuu miteru n da.
example.ja: この番組、毎週見てるんだ。
example.english: I watch this show every week.

examplePolite.romaji: kono bangumi wa maishuu mite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: この番組は毎週見ています。
examplePolite.english: I watch this show every week.

items.use: X no fan = a fan of X; daifan = a huge fan.

example.romaji: watashi, kono bando no daifan nan da.
example.ja: 私、このバンドの大ファンなんだ。
example.english: I'm a huge fan of this band.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi, kono bando no daifan nan desu.
examplePolite.ja: 私、このバンドの大ファンなんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm a huge fan of this band.

items.notes: Not an electric fan; that's senpuuki.

items.use: For a creator's films, books, art or anime; sounds a bit formal or fan-like.

example.romaji: kono kantoku no sakuhin, zenbu mita yo.
example.ja: この監督の作品、全部見たよ。
example.english: I've seen all of this director's films.

examplePolite.romaji: kono kantoku no sakuhin wa zenbu mimashita.
examplePolite.ja: この監督の作品は全部見ました。
examplePolite.english: I've seen all of this director's films.

blocks.label: Half and the rest
blocks.rationale: Talk about part of something and what's left.
blocks.interference: Ichibu is 'some of' a whole; bubun is a specific part.

example.ja: 半分食べていいよ。
example.english: You can have half.

examplePolite.romaji: hanbun tabete ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 半分食べていいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Please, have half.

items.notes: For 'half past' use han, as in sanji han; hanbun ni suru = split in half.

example.ja: 残りは明日やる。
example.english: I'll do the rest tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: nokori wa ashita yarimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 残りは明日やります。
examplePolite.english: I'll do the rest tomorrow.

items.notes: From nokoru (be left over). Leftover food is nokorimono.

items.use: A part of a group or whole, often 'some people': ichibu no hito.

example.ja: 一部の人しか知らない。
example.english: Only some people know.

examplePolite.romaji: ichibu no hito shika shirimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 一部の人しか知りません。
examplePolite.english: Only some people know.

items.notes: Also 'one copy' of a document or magazine.

example.ja: この部分がよくわからない。
example.english: I don't really get this part.

examplePolite.romaji: kono bubun ga yoku wakarimasen.
examplePolite.ja: この部分がよくわかりません。
examplePolite.english: I don't quite understand this part.

items.notes: A specific part you can point at; ichibu is 'some of' a whole.

blocks.label: Both, each, everything
blocks.rationale: Say both, each and all of something.
blocks.interference: Ryouhou is only for two; zentai is the whole as one, subete every part of it.

example.romaji: dotchi mo ii kara, ryouhou kau.
example.ja: どっちもいいから、両方買う。
example.english: They're both nice, so I'll buy both.

examplePolite.romaji: dochira mo ii node, ryouhou kaimasu.
examplePolite.ja: どちらもいいので、両方買います。
examplePolite.english: They're both nice, so I'll take both.

items.notes: Only for two things; for three or more use zenbu.

items.use: Stresses that each person or thing is separate or different.

example.ja: みんなそれぞれ違うからね。
example.english: Everyone's different, you know.

examplePolite.romaji: minna sorezore chigaimasu kara ne.
examplePolite.ja: みんなそれぞれ違いますからね。
examplePolite.english: Everyone is different, after all.

items.use: Sounds a bit serious or written; in everyday talk zenbu is more usual.

example.romaji: okane ga subete ja nai yo.
example.ja: お金が全てじゃないよ。
example.english: Money isn't everything.

examplePolite.romaji: okane ga subete ja arimasen yo.
examplePolite.ja: お金が全てじゃありませんよ。
examplePolite.english: Money isn't everything.

items.notes: Also works as an adverb: subete owatta = it's all done.

items.use: An emotional 'everything', often when it all goes wrong or you're fed up.

example.romaji: mou nanimo kamo iya ni natta.
example.ja: もう何もかも嫌になった。
example.english: I'm sick of everything.

examplePolite.romaji: mou nanimo kamo iya ni narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: もう何もかも嫌になりました。
examplePolite.english: I've had enough of everything.

items.notes: Not nanimo alone, which takes a negative and means 'nothing'.

items.use: Something seen as one whole; zentaiteki ni = overall, on the whole.

example.ja: 全体的にはよかったよ。
example.english: Overall it was good.

examplePolite.romaji: zentaiteki ni wa yokatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: 全体的にはよかったです。
examplePolite.english: On the whole, it was good.

items.notes: Zenbu counts every item; zentai looks at the whole as one.

blocks.label: That thing, copying, impulse
blocks.rationale: Refer to 'that thing', copying, acting on impulse and harsh people.
blocks.interference: Rei no is 'that one'; rei alone is 'example'.

items.english: that (you know the one); the usual
items.use: Points to something you both already know about, without naming it.

example.ja: 例の件、どうなった？
example.english: So what happened with that thing?

examplePolite.romaji: rei no ken wa dou narimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 例の件はどうなりましたか？
examplePolite.english: What happened with that matter we discussed?

items.notes: Rei alone means 'example': rei o ageru = give an example.

items.english: copy; imitate; do an impression of

example.ja: 私のまねしないでよ！
example.english: Stop copying me!

examplePolite.romaji: watashi no mane o shinaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 私のまねをしないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't copy me.

items.notes: The noun mane also means a stunt or behaviour: baka na mane = something stupid.

items.use: Ikioi de = on impulse, carried along by the mood.

example.ja: つい勢いで買っちゃった。
example.english: I just bought it on impulse.

examplePolite.romaji: tsui ikioi de katte shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: つい勢いで買ってしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I got carried away and bought it.

items.notes: Also physical force, like rushing water: ikioi yoku = with force, vigorously.

items.english: ogre; demon; a harsh, relentless person; 'it' in tag
items.use: In talk it often means someone merciless: oni kyoushi = a brutally strict teacher.

example.romaji: ano senpai, maji de oni da yo.
example.ja: あの先輩、マジで鬼だよ。
example.english: That senior is seriously ruthless.

examplePolite.romaji: ano senpai wa hontou ni oni desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの先輩は本当に鬼ですよ。
examplePolite.english: That senior is really harsh.

items.notes: Onigokko is the game of tag. Slang prefix for 'super': onikawa = super cute.

blocks.label: Tough and tiring
blocks.rationale: Lets you complain that something is a pain, hard, or wearing you out.
blocks.interference: Tsurai, kitsui and shindoi overlap; kurushii leans physical (breathing, too full).

items.english: what a pain; such a hassle; can't be bothered
items.use: The everyday grumble about chores; of a person, 'mendokusai hito' = a difficult, high-maintenance person.

example.ja: 料理するの、めんどくさいな。
example.english: Cooking is such a pain.

examplePolite.romaji: ryouri suru no wa mendokusai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 料理するのはめんどくさいですね。
examplePolite.english: Cooking is such a hassle, isn't it?

items.notes: Spoken form of mendoukusai; often cut further to mendoi. The noun mendou (hassle) sounds softer in polite talk.

items.use: For things that hurt or wear you down: a breakup, a hard job, getting up early.

example.romaji: asa hayaku okiru no, tsurai na.
example.ja: 朝早く起きるの、つらいな。
example.english: Getting up early is rough.

examplePolite.romaji: asa hayaku okiru no wa tsurai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 朝早く起きるのはつらいです。
examplePolite.english: Getting up early is hard for me.

items.notes: The kanji 辛い is also read karai (spicy); in speech the meaning is clear.

items.use: For anything demanding: a hard workout, a packed schedule, tight shoes.

example.ja: この仕事、けっこうきついよ。
example.english: This job is pretty tough.

examplePolite.romaji: kono shigoto wa kekkou kitsui desu.
examplePolite.ja: この仕事はけっこうきついです。
examplePolite.english: This job is pretty tough.

items.notes: Zubon ga kitsui = my trousers are tight. Kitsui iikata = a harsh way of putting it.

items.use: Covers both a draining task and how drained you feel: 'kyou shindoi' = I'm wiped today.

example.ja: 今日は残業でしんどかった。
example.english: Today was exhausting with all the overtime.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa zangyou de shindokatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は残業でしんどかったです。
examplePolite.english: Today was exhausting with all the overtime.

items.notes: Started in Kansai, now used everywhere. Close to tsurai and kitsui, but more about fatigue.

items.english: painful; hard to breathe; hard to bear
items.use: Strain you are struggling under: a tight chest, being too full, money trouble.

example.ja: 食べすぎてお腹が苦しい。
example.english: I ate too much, I'm painfully full.

examplePolite.romaji: tabesugite onaka ga kurushii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 食べすぎてお腹が苦しいです。
examplePolite.english: I ate too much, I'm painfully full.

items.notes: Tsurai is emotional hardship; kurushii leans physical. Kurushii iiwake = a lame excuse.

blocks.label: Serious or sloppy
blocks.rationale: Lets you say whether someone takes things seriously or half-heartedly.
blocks.interference: Majime (personality) vs shinken (in the moment); tekitou and iikagen both mean sloppy, iikagen more blaming.

items.use: Hard-working and rule-following; can also mean a bit too straight-laced.

example.romaji: kare, honto ni majime da yo ne.
example.ja: 彼、ほんとにまじめだよね。
example.english: He's really conscientious, isn't he?

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa hontou ni majime desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は本当にまじめですね。
examplePolite.english: He's really conscientious, isn't he?
