examplePolite.english: Tonight it's just the women drinking.

items.notes: Pairs with danshi. joshikai = a girls' night out.

items.use: Used casually for males of any age, and in school and sports for the boys' side.

example.romaji: danshi tte, honto kodomo da yo ne.
example.ja: 男子って、ほんと子供だよね。
example.english: Guys are such kids, right?

examplePolite.romaji: danshi tte hontou ni kodomo desu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 男子って本当に子供ですよね。
examplePolite.english: Guys really are like kids, aren't they?

items.notes: Pairs with joshi.

items.use: Casual and a bit rude; men also use it about themselves as a joke.

example.romaji: mou ossan da kara, tetsuya muri.
example.ja: もうおっさんだから、徹夜無理。
example.english: I'm an old man now, I can't pull all-nighters.

items.notes: The politer word is ojisan; for women, obasan.

blocks.label: Babies kids and age
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about babies, kids, young people and who is older.
blocks.interference: gaki is rude; the neutral word for a kid is kodomo.

example.romaji: akachan neteru kara, shizuka ni ne.
example.ja: 赤ちゃん寝てるから、静かにね。
example.english: The baby's asleep, so keep it down.

examplePolite.romaji: akachan ga nete iru node, shizuka ni shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 赤ちゃんが寝ているので、静かにしてください。
examplePolite.english: The baby is sleeping, so please be quiet.

items.notes: Also for baby animals: neko no akachan (a kitten).

items.use: Often X no hou ga toshiue (X is older) or toshiue no hito (an older person).

example.romaji: kanojo, futatsu toshiue na n da.
example.ja: 彼女、二つ年上なんだ。
example.english: She's two years older than me.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo wa futatsu toshiue desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女は二つ年上です。
examplePolite.english: She's two years older than me.

items.notes: Opposite: toshishita (younger).

items.use: Rough and often insulting; also used to call an adult childish.

example.ja: お前、まだガキだな。
example.english: You're still such a kid.

items.notes: The neutral word is kodomo.

items.use: Young people as a group, often said by older people or the media.

example.romaji: saikin no wakamono wa terebi minai yo ne.
example.ja: 最近の若者はテレビ見ないよね。
example.english: Young people these days don't watch TV, right?

examplePolite.romaji: saikin no wakamono wa terebi o mimasen ne.
examplePolite.ja: 最近の若者はテレビを見ませんね。
examplePolite.english: Young people these days don't watch TV.

items.notes: wakai hito is the softer everyday way to say it.

blocks.label: Titles at work
blocks.rationale: Job titles that also work as names to call someone by.
blocks.interference: buchou ranks above kachou; mixing them up is awkward.

items.english: company president; head of a company
items.use: Also used like a name to address the president directly.

example.ja: 社長もう帰った？
example.english: Has the boss gone home already?

examplePolite.romaji: shachou wa mou kaerimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 社長はもう帰りましたか？
examplePolite.english: Has the president gone home already?

items.notes: Owners of small businesses are called shachou too.

items.english: department head; head of a school club
items.use: Used like a name to address them, and for the head of a school club.

example.ja: 部長が呼んでるよ。
example.english: The manager wants you.

examplePolite.romaji: buchou ga yonde imasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 部長が呼んでいますよ。
examplePolite.english: The department head is asking for you.

items.notes: Sits above kachou and below shachou.

items.use: Used like a name to address the manager at shops and restaurants.

example.ja: 店長に聞いてくるね。
example.english: I'll go ask the manager.

examplePolite.romaji: tenchou ni kiite kimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 店長に聞いてきます。
examplePolite.english: I'll go and ask the manager.

items.use: A mid-level manager; also used like a name to address them.

example.ja: 課長、今日休みだって。
example.english: Apparently the section chief is off today.

examplePolite.romaji: kachou wa kyou yasumi da sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 課長は今日休みだそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear the section chief is off today.

items.notes: Ranks below buchou.

items.english: film director; team manager or coach
items.use: Also used like a name to address the director or coach.

example.romaji: ano eiga no kantoku, dare dattakke?
example.ja: あの映画の監督、誰だったっけ？
example.english: Who directed that movie again?

examplePolite.romaji: ano eiga no kantoku wa dare deshitakke?
examplePolite.ja: あの映画の監督は誰でしたっけ？
examplePolite.english: Who was the director of that movie again?

items.notes: As kantoku suru it means to supervise.

blocks.label: School stages
blocks.rationale: Lets you say what stage of school someone is in.
blocks.interference: chuugakusei (middle) and koukousei (high) sound alike.

items.use: Ages about 6 to 12.

example.romaji: musuko, mada shougakusei na n da.
example.ja: 息子、まだ小学生なんだ。
example.english: My son's still in elementary school.

examplePolite.romaji: musuko wa mada shougakusei desu.
examplePolite.ja: 息子はまだ小学生です。
examplePolite.english: My son is still in elementary school.

items.use: Ages about 12 to 15.

example.ja: 中学生の時、サッカーやってた。
example.english: I played soccer in junior high.

examplePolite.romaji: chuugakusei no toki, sakkaa o yatte imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 中学生の時、サッカーをやっていました。
examplePolite.english: I played soccer in junior high.

items.use: Ages about 15 to 18.

example.romaji: kore, koukousei no toki no shashin.
example.ja: これ、高校生の時の写真。
example.english: This is me in high school.

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa koukousei no toki no shashin desu.
examplePolite.ja: これは高校生の時の写真です。
examplePolite.english: This is a photo from when I was in high school.

example.romaji: imouto wa ima daigakusei da yo.
example.ja: 妹は今大学生だよ。
example.english: My little sister's in college now.

examplePolite.romaji: imouto wa ima daigakusei desu.
examplePolite.ja: 妹は今大学生です。
examplePolite.english: My younger sister is at university now.

blocks.label: Dreams and reality
blocks.rationale: Lets you set ideals and miracles against harsh reality.
blocks.interference: None.

items.use: Real life as opposed to dreams, plans or fiction.

example.romaji: genjitsu wa sonna ni amakunai yo
example.ja: 現実はそんなに甘くないよ
example.english: Real life isn't that easy.

examplePolite.romaji: genjitsu wa sonna ni amaku arimasen yo
examplePolite.ja: 現実はそんなに甘くありませんよ
examplePolite.english: Real life isn't that easy.

items.notes: Genjitsu o miro = face reality. Genjitsuteki = realistic.

items.use: In quick prayers and exclamations, and as praise for someone who saved the day.

example.ja: 神様、お願い!合格させて!
example.english: Please, God, let me pass!

examplePolite.romaji: kamisama, douka goukaku dekimasu you ni
examplePolite.ja: 神様、どうか合格できますように
examplePolite.english: Please, God, let me pass.

items.notes: Slang: kami alone means 'amazing' (kami da! = that's awesome).

items.use: Your ideal of something: risou no taipu (ideal type), risou ga takai (have high standards).

example.romaji: risou no kareshi tte donna hito?
example.ja: 理想の彼氏ってどんな人?
example.english: What's your ideal boyfriend like?

examplePolite.romaji: risou no kareshi wa donna hito desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 理想の彼氏はどんな人ですか?
examplePolite.english: What would your ideal boyfriend be like?

items.notes: Often paired with genjitsu: risou to genjitsu (the ideal vs reality). Risouteki = ideal (as an adjective).

items.use: Something that by rights shouldn't have happened, often said with relief or exaggeration.

example.romaji: shiken ni ukatta no wa kiseki da yo
example.ja: 試験に受かったのは奇跡だよ
example.english: Me passing that exam was a miracle.

examplePolite.romaji: shiken ni ukatta no wa kiseki desu
examplePolite.ja: 試験に受かったのは奇跡です
examplePolite.english: Passing that exam was a miracle.

items.notes: Kiseki ga okiru = a miracle happens. Kisekiteki ni = miraculously.

blocks.label: Memories and stories
blocks.rationale: Lets you tell a memory: what happened one day and what you remember.
blocks.interference: Omoide is a fond memory; kioku is what your brain stored.

items.use: What you can recall: kioku ga nai (I don't remember), kioku o ushinau (lose your memory).

example.romaji: sono hi no kioku ga zenzen nai
example.ja: その日の記憶が全然ない
example.english: I have no memory of that day at all.

examplePolite.romaji: sono hi no kioku ga zenzen arimasen
examplePolite.ja: その日の記憶が全然ありません
examplePolite.english: I have no memory of that day at all.

items.notes: A cherished memory is omoide. Kiokuryoku = memory as a skill.

items.use: Opens a story about a past day; not for a future 'someday'.

example.romaji: aru hi, kyuu ni kare kara denwa ga kita
example.ja: ある日、急に彼から電話が来た
example.english: Then one day he suddenly called me.

examplePolite.romaji: aru hi, kyuu ni kare kara denwa ga kimashita
examplePolite.ja: ある日、急に彼から電話が来ました
examplePolite.english: Then one day he suddenly called me.

items.notes: Someday in the future is itsuka. Aru means 'a certain', as in aru hito (someone).

items.use: Any happening, big or small: kyou no dekigoto (what happened today).

example.romaji: ano dekigoto wa ima demo wasurerarenai
example.ja: あの出来事は今でも忘れられない
example.english: I still can't forget what happened that time.

examplePolite.romaji: ano dekigoto wa ima demo wasureraremasen
examplePolite.ja: あの出来事は今でも忘れられません
examplePolite.english: I still can't forget what happened that time.

items.notes: In casual speech people often just say koto: hen na koto ga atta. A planned event is ibento.

blocks.label: Before, during, last time
blocks.rationale: Lets you place things around an event: on the way, last time, right before, on the day.
blocks.interference: Toujitsu (on the day) vs touji (at the time).

items.english: on the way; in the middle (of)
items.use: Both partway along a route (kaeri no tochuu, on the way home) and partway through a task.

example.romaji: ima eki ni iku tochuu da yo
example.ja: 今駅に行く途中だよ
example.english: I'm on my way to the station now.

examplePolite.romaji: ima eki ni iku tochuu desu
examplePolite.ja: 今駅に行く途中です
examplePolite.english: I'm on my way to the station now.

items.notes: Tochuu de = partway, before finishing: tochuu de yameta (I quit halfway).

items.use: The previous meeting, episode, visit or lesson in a series.

example.ja: 前回の続きからやろう
example.english: Let's pick up where we left off last time.

examplePolite.romaji: zenkai no tsuzuki kara yarimashou
examplePolite.ja: 前回の続きからやりましょう
examplePolite.english: Let's pick up where we left off last time.

items.notes: Konkai = this time, jikai = next time. Casual 'the other time' is kono mae.

items.use: After a noun with no or a verb: shiken no chokuzen, deru chokuzen (right before leaving).

example.ja: 出かける直前に気づいた
example.english: I noticed right before I went out.

examplePolite.romaji: dekakeru chokuzen ni kizukimashita
examplePolite.ja: 出かける直前に気づきました
examplePolite.english: I noticed right before I went out.

items.notes: Opposite: chokugo (right after). Plain 'before' is mae.

items.english: on the day; the day itself
items.use: The day of a planned event: a test, trip, wedding or booking.

example.romaji: chiketto wa toujitsu demo kaeru yo
example.ja: チケットは当日でも買えるよ
example.english: You can buy tickets on the day too.

examplePolite.romaji: chiketto wa toujitsu demo kaemasu yo
examplePolite.ja: チケットは当日でも買えますよ
examplePolite.english: You can buy tickets on the day too.

items.notes: Don't mix it up with touji (at the time).

blocks.label: Special occasions
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about firsts, ceremonies and marking a day.
blocks.interference: Hatsu (first ever) vs hajimete (for the first time).

items.use: Goes before a noun for a first experience: hatsu deeto (first date), hatsu taiken (first time trying something).

example.romaji: kyou ga kanojo to no hatsu deeto da yo
example.ja: 今日が彼女との初デートだよ
example.english: Today's my first date with her.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou ga kanojo to no hatsu deeto desu
examplePolite.ja: 今日が彼女との初デートです
examplePolite.english: Today is my first date with her.

items.notes: 'For the first time' is hajimete. The same kanji is read sho in shonichi (opening day).

items.use: Short for a ceremony both people know about, usually the wedding: shiki wa itsu? (when's the wedding?).

example.romaji: shiki wa rainen no haru ni suru
example.ja: 式は来年の春にする
example.english: We're having the wedding next spring.

examplePolite.romaji: shiki wa rainen no haru ni shimasu
examplePolite.ja: 式は来年の春にします
examplePolite.english: We're holding the wedding next spring.

items.notes: Full forms: kekkonshiki (wedding), sotsugyoushiki (graduation). In compounds it can also mean 'style' or 'formula'.

items.english: commemoration; keepsake; to mark the occasion
items.use: Mostly kinen ni (as a keepsake, to mark the day) and in compounds.

example.romaji: kinen ni issho ni shashin torou yo
example.ja: 記念に一緒に写真撮ろうよ
example.english: Let's take a photo together to remember this.

examplePolite.romaji: kinen ni issho ni shashin o torimashou
examplePolite.ja: 記念に一緒に写真を撮りましょう
examplePolite.english: Let's take a photo together to mark the occasion.

items.notes: Kinenbi = anniversary. Kinen shashin = a photo to mark the day.

blocks.label: Likes and love
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about your type, your love life, jealousy and what bores you.
blocks.interference: Ren'ai is romance as a topic, not loving one person (suki).

items.use: A flat brush-off: [thing] ni kyoumi nai.

example.ja: そんな話、興味ないよ
example.english: I'm not interested in that kind of thing.

examplePolite.romaji: sou iu hanashi ni wa kyoumi arimasen
examplePolite.ja: そういう話には興味ありません
examplePolite.english: I'm not interested in that kind of thing.

items.notes: Positive: kyoumi ga aru (be interested). Said about a person, it sounds cold.

items.use: Romantic love as a topic or part of life, not a feeling toward one person.

example.romaji: ima wa ren'ai yori shigoto ga daiji
example.ja: 今は恋愛より仕事が大事
example.english: Right now work matters more than romance.

examplePolite.romaji: ima wa ren'ai yori shigoto ga daiji desu
examplePolite.ja: 今は恋愛より仕事が大事です
examplePolite.english: Right now work matters more than romance.

items.notes: Loving one person is suki or koi. Ren'ai kekkon = a love marriage.

items.use: What you like in food, style or people: watashi no konomi (my type).

example.romaji: kare, kanzen ni watashi no konomi
example.ja: 彼、完全に私の好み
example.english: He's totally my type.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa kanzen ni watashi no konomi desu
examplePolite.ja: 彼は完全に私の好みです
examplePolite.english: He's totally my type.

items.notes: Konomi ja nai = not my thing. For people, taipu is just as common.

items.use: Jealousy in love, and envy of someone's success.

example.ja: 別に嫉妬してないし
example.english: It's not like I'm jealous or anything.

examplePolite.romaji: betsu ni shitto shite imasen yo
examplePolite.ja: 別に嫉妬していませんよ
examplePolite.english: I'm not jealous, you know.

items.notes: Casual alternative: yakimochi o yaku. Urayamashii is the lighter 'I envy you'.

blocks.label: Talent and skill
blocks.rationale: Lets you praise or judge what someone can do.
blocks.interference: All three translate as 'ability': sainou is inborn, jitsuryoku is proven, nouryoku is general.

items.use: A natural gift: ~ no sainou ga aru (have a talent for ~).

example.romaji: e no sainou aru yo ne
example.ja: 絵の才能あるよね
example.english: You've really got a talent for drawing.

examplePolite.romaji: e no sainou ga arimasu ne
examplePolite.ja: 絵の才能がありますね
examplePolite.english: You have a real talent for drawing.

items.notes: Sainou is inborn; jitsuryoku is proven skill; nouryoku is ability in general.

items.use: Ability in general, often for work or study; in dramas also superpowers.

example.romaji: kare wa nouryoku wa takai kedo, yaru ki ga nai
example.ja: 彼は能力は高いけど、やる気がない
example.english: He's very capable, but he's got no drive.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa nouryoku wa takai desu ga, yaru ki ga arimasen
examplePolite.ja: 彼は能力は高いですが、やる気がありません
examplePolite.english: He's very capable, but he has no drive.

items.notes: Chounouryoku = supernatural powers. Day to day, 'can do' is just dekiru.

items.use: The skill you actually show, in contests or at work; often set against luck.

example.romaji: un ja nakute jitsuryoku da yo
example.ja: 運じゃなくて実力だよ
example.english: That wasn't luck, that was skill.

examplePolite.romaji: un de wa naku jitsuryoku desu yo
examplePolite.ja: 運ではなく実力ですよ
examplePolite.english: That wasn't luck, that was real skill.

items.notes: Jitsuryoku o dasu = perform at your true level.

blocks.label: Sensing and feeling
blocks.rationale: Lets you say something feels off, you've got a hunch, or you can't feel your hands.
blocks.interference: Kankaku (sensation) vs kanjou (emotion), both 'feeling' in English.

items.use: Usually iwakan ga aru: something feels wrong or not quite right, in a situation or in your body.

example.romaji: atarashii megane, mada chotto iwakan ga aru
example.ja: 新しいメガネ、まだちょっと違和感がある
example.english: My new glasses still feel a bit weird.

examplePolite.romaji: atarashii megane, mada chotto iwakan ga arimasu
examplePolite.ja: 新しいメガネ、まだちょっと違和感があります
examplePolite.english: My new glasses still feel a little strange.

items.notes: Also for stories or behavior that don't add up: kare no hanashi ni iwakan ga aru (something's off about his story).

items.use: Being conscious (ishiki ga nai, he's out cold) and being aware of something (~ o ishiki suru).

example.ja: 彼、まだ意識が戻らない
example.english: He still hasn't come round.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa mada ishiki ga modorimasen
examplePolite.ja: 彼はまだ意識が戻りません
examplePolite.english: He still hasn't regained consciousness.

items.notes: Ishiki shiteru = be conscious of someone, often a hint of a crush. Muishiki ni = without thinking.

items.use: Emotions as a whole, often about showing or holding them in; 'how I feel' right now is kimochi.

example.romaji: kare wa kanjou o kao ni dasanai
example.ja: 彼は感情を顔に出さない
example.english: He doesn't let his feelings show on his face.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa kanjou o kao ni dashimasen
examplePolite.ja: 彼は感情を顔に出しません
examplePolite.english: He doesn't let his feelings show on his face.

items.notes: Kanjouteki ni naru = get emotional. Same sound as kanjou, the bill at a restaurant.

items.use: Physical sensation (te no kankaku ga nai, no feeling in my hand) and a feel for things.

example.romaji: samusugite yubi no kankaku ga nai
example.ja: 寒すぎて指の感覚がない
example.english: It's so cold I can't feel my fingers.

examplePolite.romaji: samusugite yubi no kankaku ga arimasen
examplePolite.ja: 寒すぎて指の感覚がありません
examplePolite.english: It's so cold I can't feel my fingers.

items.notes: Kankaku de = by feel, by instinct. Emotions are kanjou, not kankaku.

items.use: Almost always ~ yokan ga suru: iya na yokan ga suru (I've got a bad feeling).

example.romaji: nanka iya na yokan ga suru
example.ja: なんか嫌な予感がする
example.english: I've got a bad feeling about this.

examplePolite.romaji: nandaka iya na yokan ga shimasu
examplePolite.ja: なんだか嫌な予感がします
examplePolite.english: I have a bad feeling about this.

items.notes: Ii yokan = a good feeling about it. Yokan ga ataru = your hunch turns out right.

blocks.label: Goals and plans
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about what you're aiming for and what comes first.
blocks.interference: Mokuteki is the purpose; mokuhyou is the target you aim to hit.

items.use: Nan no mokuteki de? = what for?, often suspicious.

example.romaji: nan no mokuteki de sonna koto suru no?
example.ja: 何の目的でそんなことするの？
example.english: What are you doing that for?

examplePolite.romaji: nan no mokuteki de sonna koto o suru n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 何の目的でそんなことをするんですか？
examplePolite.english: What's the purpose of doing that?

items.notes: Mokuteki is the purpose; mokuhyou is a target you aim to hit.

items.use: A military word used playfully for any plan, like winning someone over.

example.ja: じゃあ、明日の作戦立てよう。
example.english: Okay, let's work out a plan for tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: dewa, ashita no sakusen o tatemashou.
examplePolite.ja: では、明日の作戦を立てましょう。
examplePolite.english: Right, let's work out a plan for tomorrow.

items.notes: Keikaku is the neutral word for a plan or schedule.

items.use: A concrete thing you aim for, often with a number or a date.

example.romaji: kotoshi no mokuhyou wa go kiro yaseru koto.
example.ja: 今年の目標は5キロ痩せること。
example.english: My goal this year is to lose five kilos.

examplePolite.romaji: kotoshi no mokuhyou wa go kiro yaseru koto desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今年の目標は5キロ痩せることです。
examplePolite.english: My goal this year is to lose five kilos.

items.use: Usually 'X o yuusen suru' (put X first).

example.romaji: ima wa kenkou o yuusen shita hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: 今は健康を優先した方がいいよ。
example.english: Right now you should put your health first.

examplePolite.romaji: ima wa kenkou o yuusen shita hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 今は健康を優先した方がいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Right now you should put your health first.

items.notes: As a noun: yuusen seki (priority seat), yuusen jun'i (order of priority).

blocks.label: How things unfold
blocks.rationale: Lets you tell how a situation went and where it stands now.
blocks.interference: Nagare is the general flow; tenkai is a twist or turn in it.

items.english: how things went; flow; the course of events
items.use: Nagare de = as things went, to explain how something just happened.

example.romaji: nagare de nomi ni iku koto ni natta.
example.ja: 流れで飲みに行くことになった。
example.english: We just ended up going for drinks.

examplePolite.romaji: nagare de nomi ni iku koto ni narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 流れで飲みに行くことになりました。
examplePolite.english: We just ended up going for drinks.

items.notes: Also a literal flow, of a river or traffic; the verb is nagareru (flow).

items.english: turn of events; how a story develops
items.use: Common about TV, films and real life: masaka no tenkai = an unexpected twist.

example.romaji: sono tenkai wa yosou shite nakatta.
example.ja: その展開は予想してなかった。
example.english: I didn't see that coming.

examplePolite.romaji: sono tenkai wa yosou shite imasen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: その展開は予想していませんでした。
examplePolite.english: I didn't see that coming.

items.notes: Tenkai suru = unfold; in business, expand (a chain of shops).

items.use: Ketsuron kara iu to = to cut to the chase, long story short.

example.romaji: ketsuron kara iu to, dame datta.
example.ja: 結論から言うと、ダメだった。
example.english: Long story short, it didn't work out.

examplePolite.romaji: ketsuron kara iu to, dame deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 結論から言うと、ダメでした。
examplePolite.english: To cut to the chase, it didn't work out.

items.use: Often 'ima no dankai de wa' (at this stage) when nothing's decided yet.

example.ja: まだ考えてる段階だよ。
example.english: I'm still at the thinking stage.

examplePolite.romaji: mada kangaete iru dankai desu.
examplePolite.ja: まだ考えている段階です。
examplePolite.english: I'm still at the thinking stage.

blocks.label: Chatting and topics
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about chatting and what to talk about.
blocks.interference: Neta is something to talk about; wadai is the topic itself.

items.use: Usually 'oshaberi suru' (to chat).

example.ja: カフェでずっとおしゃべりしてた。
example.english: We sat chatting in a café the whole time.

examplePolite.romaji: kafe de zutto oshaberi shite imashita.
examplePolite.ja: カフェでずっとおしゃべりしていました。
examplePolite.english: We sat chatting in a café the whole time.

items.notes: Said of a person it means a chatterbox or someone who can't keep a secret, often as a light tease.

items.use: Sounds a little formal; in casual talk people mostly just say hanasu (talk).

example.romaji: kare to zenzen kaiwa ga tsuzukanai.
example.ja: 彼と全然会話が続かない。
example.english: I can never keep a conversation going with him.

examplePolite.romaji: kare to wa zenzen kaiwa ga tsuzukimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 彼とは全然会話が続きません。
examplePolite.english: I can never keep a conversation going with him.

items.notes: Eikaiwa = English conversation (lessons).

items.english: something to talk about; material, a joke
items.use: Casual word for a story, topic or joke you can use.

example.ja: 話すネタがなくなった。
example.english: I've run out of things to talk about.

examplePolite.romaji: hanasu neta ga nakunarimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 話すネタがなくなりました。
examplePolite.english: I've run out of things to talk about.

items.notes: Netabare = spoiler; neta is also the fish on top of sushi.

items.use: Wadai no X = the much-talked-about X; wadai ni naru = become the talk of the town.

example.ja: ちょっと話題変えようか。
example.english: Let's change the subject.

examplePolite.romaji: chotto wadai o kaemashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっと話題を変えましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we change the subject?

blocks.label: Where you live
blocks.rationale: Lets you say where you live and where you're from.
blocks.interference: Katei is the household, not the building (ie or uchi).

items.use: Inaka ni kaeru means going back to your family's home region.

example.romaji: oshougatsu wa inaka ni kaeru yo.
example.ja: お正月は田舎に帰るよ。
example.english: I'm going back home to the country for New Year.

examplePolite.romaji: oshougatsu wa inaka ni kaerimasu.
examplePolite.ja: お正月は田舎に帰ります。
examplePolite.english: I'm going back home to the country for New Year.

items.notes: Calling a place inaka can sound mildly dismissive, like 'the sticks'.

example.ja: 住所、あとで送ってね。
example.english: Send me your address later, okay?

examplePolite.romaji: juusho o ato de okutte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 住所をあとで送ってください。
examplePolite.english: Please send me your address later.

items.notes: Not for email: an email address is a meeru adoresu.

example.romaji: ima eki no chikaku no apaato ni sunderu.
example.ja: 今、駅の近くのアパートに住んでる。
example.english: I'm living in a flat near the station now.

examplePolite.romaji: ima eki no chikaku no apaato ni sunde imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今、駅の近くのアパートに住んでいます。
examplePolite.english: I'm living in a flat near the station now.

items.notes: A newer, sturdier block of flats is a manshon, which doesn't mean mansion.

items.use: Home as a family unit, not the building (that's ie or uchi).

example.romaji: kare, katei no jijou de yameta rashii yo.
example.ja: 彼、家庭の事情で辞めたらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently he quit for family reasons.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa katei no jijou de yameta sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は家庭の事情で辞めたそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear he quit for family reasons.

items.notes: Kateiteki (homely, good at home life) is a compliment.

blocks.label: Meeting new people
blocks.rationale: Lets you introduce yourself, say where you're from and swap contacts.
blocks.interference: Shusshin is where you're from; jimoto is where you grew up or live now.

items.use: The place you grew up, or the area you live in now; jimoto no = local.

example.romaji: oshougatsu wa jimoto ni kaeru yo.
example.ja: お正月は地元に帰るよ。
example.english: I'm going back home for New Year.

examplePolite.romaji: oshougatsu wa jimoto ni kaerimasu.
examplePolite.ja: お正月は地元に帰ります。
examplePolite.english: I'm going back home for New Year.

items.notes: Jimoto no tomodachi = friends from back home.

items.use: Usually 'X shusshin' (from X); doko shusshin? is the standard 'where are you from?'.

example.romaji: tanaka-san tte, doko shusshin na no?
example.ja: 田中さんって、どこ出身なの？
example.english: Tanaka, where are you from?

examplePolite.romaji: tanaka-san wa doko no shusshin desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 田中さんはどこの出身ですか？
examplePolite.english: Where are you from, Mr Tanaka?

items.notes: Also the school you graduated from: Toudai shusshin (a Tokyo University graduate).

items.use: Usually 'jikoshoukai suru' (introduce yourself); expected at first meetings, classes and new jobs.

example.ja: じゃあ、まず自己紹介しようか。
example.english: Okay, let's start by introducing ourselves.

examplePolite.romaji: dewa, mazu jikoshoukai o shimashou.
examplePolite.ja: では、まず自己紹介をしましょう。
examplePolite.english: Well then, let's start with introductions.

items.use: Your number, LINE or email; renrakusaki koukan = swapping contacts, usually on LINE.

example.ja: よかったら連絡先交換しない？
example.english: Want to swap contacts?

examplePolite.romaji: yokattara renrakusaki o koukan shimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: よかったら連絡先を交換しませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like to exchange contact details?

items.notes: Renraku suru = get in touch.

blocks.label: Buildings and institutions
blocks.rationale: Lets you point out buildings, the stairs inside, and places like kindergartens and care homes.
blocks.interference: Biru is a building, never a bill to pay.

example.romaji: musume, rainen kara youchien da yo.
example.ja: 娘、来年から幼稚園だよ。
example.english: My daughter starts kindergarten next year.

examplePolite.romaji: musume wa rainen kara youchien desu.
examplePolite.ja: 娘は来年から幼稚園です。
examplePolite.english: My daughter starts kindergarten next year.

items.notes: Daycare for younger children or working parents is hoikuen.

items.use: A modern block of offices or shops, not a house; tatemono is the general word.

example.romaji: ano biru no sangai ni aru yo.
example.ja: あのビルの三階にあるよ。
example.english: It's on the third floor of that building.

examplePolite.romaji: ano biru no sangai ni arimasu.
examplePolite.ja: あのビルの三階にあります。
examplePolite.english: It's on the third floor of that building.

items.notes: Not 'bill': the bill at a restaurant is okaikei.

example.romaji: erebeetaa konderu kara, kaidan de ikou.
example.ja: エレベーター混んでるから、階段で行こう。
example.english: The lift's packed, so let's take the stairs.

examplePolite.romaji: erebeetaa ga konde iru node, kaidan de ikimashou.
examplePolite.ja: エレベーターが混んでいるので、階段で行きましょう。
examplePolite.english: The lift is crowded, so let's take the stairs.

items.notes: Go up = kaidan o noboru; go down = kaidan o oriru.

items.use: Shisetsu ni hairu usually means moving into a care home.

example.romaji: obaachan, kyonen kara shisetsu ni haitteru n da.
example.ja: おばあちゃん、去年から施設に入ってるんだ。
example.english: My grandma's been in a care home since last year.

examplePolite.romaji: sobo wa kyonen kara shisetsu ni haitte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 祖母は去年から施設に入っています。
examplePolite.english: My grandmother has been in a care home since last year.

items.notes: In dramas it often means the children's home someone grew up in.

blocks.label: Phone and gadgets
blocks.rationale: Lets you swap numbers and talk about your phone, watch and camera.
blocks.interference: Tokei is both a clock and a watch.

items.use: Short for keitai denwa; many people now just say sumaho.

example.ja: 携帯、家に忘れちゃった。
example.english: I left my phone at home.

examplePolite.romaji: keitai o ie ni wasurete shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 携帯を家に忘れてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I've left my phone at home.

example.ja: 電話番号教えてくれる?
example.english: Can you give me your number?

examplePolite.romaji: denwa bangou o oshiete itadakemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 電話番号を教えていただけますか?
examplePolite.english: Could I have your phone number?

items.notes: Often just bangou in context; give your number = oshieru.

items.use: Covers both; udedokei means a wristwatch specifically.

example.ja: あの時計、ちょっと進んでるよ。
example.english: That clock's a bit fast.

examplePolite.romaji: ano tokei wa sukoshi susunde imasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの時計は少し進んでいますよ。
examplePolite.english: That clock is a little fast.

items.notes: Fast = susunde iru; slow = okurete iru.

example.ja: 新しいカメラ買ったんだ。
example.english: I bought a new camera.

examplePolite.romaji: atarashii kamera o kaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 新しいカメラを買いました。
examplePolite.english: I bought a new camera.

items.notes: Take a photo = shashin o toru.

blocks.label: Doors and windows
blocks.rationale: Lets you open up, shut up and say where something was left.
blocks.interference: Genkan is a home's entrance; a building's is iriguchi.

example.ja: 寒いからドア閉めてくれる?
example.english: It's cold, can you shut the door?

examplePolite.romaji: samui node doa o shimete moraemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 寒いのでドアを閉めてもらえますか?
examplePolite.english: It's cold, could you shut the door?

items.notes: Open = akeru, shut = shimeru.

example.ja: ちょっと窓開けてもいい?
example.english: Mind if I open the window a bit?

examplePolite.romaji: sukoshi mado o akete mo ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 少し窓を開けてもいいですか?
examplePolite.english: May I open the window a little?

items.notes: A window seat is madogawa no seki.

items.use: The entry area of a home where you take your shoes off, a step below the floor.

example.romaji: nimotsu, genkan ni oite oku ne.
example.ja: 荷物、玄関に置いておくね。
example.english: I'll leave the parcel by the front door.

examplePolite.romaji: nimotsu wa genkan ni oite okimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 荷物は玄関に置いておきますね。
examplePolite.english: I'll leave the parcel by the front door.

items.notes: Mainly for homes; a building's entrance is the iriguchi.

example.romaji: shuumatsu, niwa de baabekyuu shiyou yo.
example.ja: 週末、庭でバーベキューしようよ。
example.english: Let's have a barbecue in the garden this weekend.

examplePolite.romaji: shuumatsu, niwa de baabekyuu o shimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 週末、庭でバーベキューをしましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's have a barbecue in the garden this weekend.

items.notes: A house's own garden; a public park is a kouen.

blocks.label: Before you go out
blocks.rationale: Lets you check you've got everything before leaving.
blocks.interference: Kagi means both key and lock.

items.use: Covers the lock too: kagi o kakeru = lock it, kagi o akeru = unlock it.

example.ja: 鍵、どこに置いたっけ?
example.english: Where did I put the keys?

examplePolite.romaji: kagi wa doko ni okimashitakke?
examplePolite.ja: 鍵はどこに置きましたっけ?
examplePolite.english: Where did I put the keys?

example.ja: やばい、財布落としたかも。
example.english: Oh no, I think I dropped my wallet.

examplePolite.romaji: saifu o otoshita kamo shiremasen.
examplePolite.ja: 財布を落としたかもしれません。
examplePolite.english: I may have dropped my wallet.

example.romaji: ame furisou da kara, kasa motte itte.
example.ja: 雨降りそうだから、傘持って行って。
example.english: It looks like rain, so take an umbrella.

examplePolite.romaji: ame ga furisou desu kara, kasa o motte itte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 雨が降りそうですから、傘を持って行ってください。
examplePolite.english: It looks like rain, so please take an umbrella.

items.notes: Put up an umbrella = kasa o sasu.

example.ja: 眼鏡、すごく似合うね。
example.english: Glasses really suit you.

examplePolite.romaji: megane, totemo niaimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 眼鏡、とても似合いますね。
examplePolite.english: Glasses really suit you.

items.notes: Wear glasses = megane o kakeru, not kiru. Often written メガネ.

items.use: Wasuremono nai? is the standard 'Got everything?' before leaving.

example.ja: 忘れ物ない?じゃあ、行くよ。
example.english: Got everything? Okay, let's go.

examplePolite.romaji: wasuremono wa nai desu ka? jaa, ikimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 忘れ物はないですか?じゃあ、行きましょう。
examplePolite.english: Have you got everything? Okay, let's go.

items.notes: Trains and shops announce owasuremono ni go-chuui kudasai: mind you don't leave anything.

blocks.label: Meat, fish and vegetables
blocks.rationale: Lets you say what you eat and shop for.
blocks.interference: None.

example.romaji: kyou wa niku ga tabetai na
example.ja: 今日は肉が食べたいな
example.english: I feel like eating meat today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa niku ga tabetai desu
examplePolite.ja: 今日は肉が食べたいです
examplePolite.english: I'd like to eat meat today.

items.notes: Beef is gyuuniku, pork butaniku, chicken toriniku.

example.romaji: sakana anmari suki ja nai n da
example.ja: 魚あんまり好きじゃないんだ
example.english: I'm not really into fish.

examplePolite.romaji: sakana wa amari suki ja nai n desu
examplePolite.ja: 魚はあまり好きじゃないんです
examplePolite.english: I don't really like fish.

example.ja: 野菜もちゃんと食べてね
example.english: Make sure you eat your vegetables too.

examplePolite.romaji: yasai mo chanto tabete kudasai ne
examplePolite.ja: 野菜もちゃんと食べてくださいね
examplePolite.english: Please make sure you eat your vegetables too.

example.ja: 果物なら何が好き?
example.english: What fruit do you like?

examplePolite.romaji: kudamono nara nani ga suki desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 果物なら何が好きですか?
examplePolite.english: What fruit do you like?

items.notes: Furuutsu is also used, mostly for desserts and drinks.

blocks.label: Water, tea and coffee
blocks.rationale: Lets you offer and ask for everyday hot and cold drinks.
blocks.interference: Omizu is cold or room-temperature water; hot water is always oyu.

items.use: On its own it means Japanese green tea; black tea is koucha.

example.ja: ちょっとお茶でも飲もうか
example.english: Shall we grab a cup of tea?

examplePolite.romaji: chotto ocha demo nomimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: ちょっとお茶でも飲みませんか?
examplePolite.english: Would you like to grab a cup of tea?

items.notes: Ocha suru means going to a cafe for a drink, whatever you order.

example.romaji: asa wa itsumo koohii nomu yo
example.ja: 朝はいつもコーヒー飲むよ
example.english: I always have coffee in the morning.

examplePolite.romaji: asa wa itsumo koohii o nomimasu
examplePolite.ja: 朝はいつもコーヒーを飲みます
examplePolite.english: I always have coffee in the morning.

items.notes: Iced coffee is aisu koohii; a hot one is hotto.

items.use: The polite way to say mizu; what you ask for at a restaurant.

example.ja: ちょっとお水もらってもいい?
example.english: Can I get some water?

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, omizu o kudasai
examplePolite.ja: すみません、お水をください
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, could I have some water?

items.notes: Mizu is always cold or room-temperature water, never hot.

items.use: Japanese has its own word for hot water; don't say atsui mizu.

example.ja: ちょっとお湯沸かしてくれる?
example.english: Can you boil some water?

examplePolite.romaji: chotto oyu o wakashite moraemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: ちょっとお湯を沸かしてもらえますか?
examplePolite.english: Could you boil some water?

items.notes: Oyu o wakasu means boil water. Also the hot water in a bath.

blocks.label: Breakfast basics
blocks.rationale: Lets you talk about breakfast and everyday groceries.
blocks.interference: Gyuunyuu is milk to drink; miruku is milk in coffee or for babies.

items.use: Covers bread, rolls and sweet buns.

example.romaji: asa wa pan to koohii dake
example.ja: 朝はパンとコーヒーだけ
example.english: Just bread and coffee for breakfast.

examplePolite.romaji: asa wa pan to koohii dake desu
examplePolite.ja: 朝はパンとコーヒーだけです
examplePolite.english: I just have bread and coffee for breakfast.

items.notes: A bakery is panya.

example.romaji: tamago ato futatsu shika nai yo
example.ja: 卵あと二つしかないよ
example.english: We've only got two eggs left.

examplePolite.romaji: tamago ga ato futatsu shika arimasen
examplePolite.ja: 卵があと二つしかありません
examplePolite.english: There are only two eggs left.

items.notes: Tamagoyaki is rolled omelette; nama tamago is raw egg, often eaten on rice.

items.use: Cow's milk you drink or buy; miruku is more for milk in coffee and for babies.

example.ja: 牛乳切れてるから買ってきて
example.english: We're out of milk, can you go buy some?

examplePolite.romaji: gyuunyuu ga kirete iru node katte kite kudasai
examplePolite.ja: 牛乳が切れているので買ってきてください
examplePolite.english: We're out of milk, so please go buy some.

example.ja: チーズのせたらおいしいよ
example.english: It's really good with cheese on top.

examplePolite.romaji: chiizu o nosetara oishii desu yo
examplePolite.ja: チーズをのせたらおいしいですよ
examplePolite.english: It's delicious with cheese on top.

items.notes: Also what you say for a photo: hai, chiizu.

blocks.label: Jobs and business
blocks.rationale: Say what work you do and who you work with.
blocks.interference: Eigyou (sales) and shoubai (trade, running a shop) both come out as 'business' in English.

items.use: The new person at work or on a team, usually in their first year.

example.romaji: kare, kotoshi no shinjin da yo.
example.ja: 彼、今年の新人だよ。
example.english: He's one of this year's new hires.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa kotoshi no shinjin desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は今年の新人です。
examplePolite.english: He's one of this year's new hires.

items.notes: Also a new face in music, film or sport. Shinjin kenshuu = training for new staff.

items.english: sales (job or department); being open for business
items.use: At a company it means sales; for a shop or restaurant it means being open.

example.romaji: eigyou no shigoto shiteru n da.
example.ja: 営業の仕事してるんだ。
example.english: I work in sales.

examplePolite.romaji: eigyou no shigoto o shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 営業の仕事をしています。
examplePolite.english: I work in sales.

items.notes: Eigyou chuu = open now; eigyou jikan = opening hours.

items.english: to get a job; to start working at a company
items.use: For landing a full-time job, often a graduate's first; the company takes ni.

example.romaji: ani ga ginkou ni shuushoku shita n da.
example.ja: 兄が銀行に就職したんだ。
example.english: My brother got a job at a bank.

examplePolite.romaji: ani ga ginkou ni shuushoku shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 兄が銀行に就職しました。
examplePolite.english: My brother got a job at a bank.

items.notes: Shuukatsu (shuushoku katsudou) = job hunting. For a part-time job, people say baito o hajimeru.

items.use: The people working at a shop, event, show or venue; one person can be 'a sutaffu'.

example.romaji: sutaffu no hito ni kiite miyou.
example.ja: スタッフの人に聞いてみよう。
example.english: Let's ask one of the staff.

examplePolite.romaji: sutaffu no kata ni kiite mimashou.
examplePolite.ja: スタッフの方に聞いてみましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's ask a staff member.

items.use: Buying and selling, especially running a shop or small business.

example.romaji: saikin, shoubai no hou wa dou?
example.ja: 最近、商売の方はどう？
example.english: How's business been lately?

examplePolite.romaji: saikin, shoubai no hou wa dou desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 最近、商売の方はどうですか？
examplePolite.english: How's business been lately?

items.notes: Bijinesu sounds corporate; shoubai is the shopkeeper's word. Shoubai ni naranai = there's no money in it.

blocks.label: Projects and results
blocks.rationale: Talk a project through from idea to the big day and how it was rated.
blocks.interference: Kikaku (a proposal to make something) is not keikaku (a plan in general).

items.use: The job in front of you right now, like sorting, typing or packing, not your job in general.

example.romaji: ima sagyou chuu dakara, ato de ne.
example.ja: 今作業中だから、後でね。
example.english: I'm in the middle of something, so later, okay?

examplePolite.romaji: ima sagyou chuu na node, ato de onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今作業中なので、後でお願いします。
examplePolite.english: I'm in the middle of some work, so later, please.

items.notes: Shigoto is your job or work in general; sagyou is the task itself. Sagyou suru also exists.

items.english: a project; a plan for an event or product
items.use: Something someone proposes and organises, like an event, a campaign or a TV segment.

example.ja: この企画、かなり面白いね。
example.english: This project idea is pretty interesting.

examplePolite.romaji: kono kikaku wa kanari omoshiroi desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: この企画はかなり面白いですね。
examplePolite.english: This project idea is really interesting.

items.notes: Keikaku is a plan in general; kikaku is a proposal for something to make or put on. Kikaku suru = to plan an event.

items.use: Used for reviews, grades and a boss's view of your work.

example.romaji: ano mise, netto no hyouka takai yo.
example.ja: あの店、ネットの評価高いよ。
example.english: That place gets great ratings online.

examplePolite.romaji: ano mise wa netto no hyouka ga takai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの店はネットの評価が高いですよ。
examplePolite.english: That place gets great ratings online.

items.notes: Hyouka ga takai / hikui = highly / poorly rated. Hyouka suru = to rate, or to value someone's work.

items.english: the real thing; the actual performance, game or take
items.use: The moment that counts after rehearsal or practice; on set, 'honban!' means this take is for real.

example.romaji: renshuu wa yokatta kedo, honban wa kinchou suru na.
example.ja: 練習は良かったけど、本番は緊張するな。
example.english: Practice went fine, but the real thing makes me nervous.

examplePolite.romaji: renshuu wa yokatta desu kedo, honban wa kinchou shimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 練習は良かったですけど、本番は緊張しますね。
examplePolite.english: Practice went well, but the real thing makes me nervous.

items.notes: Ashita ga honban = tomorrow's the big day. Honban ni tsuyoi = good under pressure.

blocks.label: School classes
blocks.rationale: Talk about classes, tests and homework.
blocks.interference: Kumi and kurasu both mean a class; teishutsu is the formal word for dasu (hand in).

items.use: A class period you attend; jugyou ga aru = have class.

example.romaji: ashita, asa kara jugyou aru n da.
example.ja: 明日、朝から授業あるんだ。
example.english: I've got class first thing tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita wa asa kara jugyou ga arimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 明日は朝から授業があります。
examplePolite.english: I have class first thing tomorrow.

items.notes: Private lessons like piano or English are ressun. Jugyou o ukeru = take a class.

example.ja: 明日テストだから勉強しなきゃ。
example.english: I have a test tomorrow, so I need to study.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita tesuto na node, benkyou shinai to ikemasen.
examplePolite.ja: 明日テストなので、勉強しないといけません。
examplePolite.english: I have a test tomorrow, so I have to study.

items.notes: Shiken is a more formal exam, like an entrance or licence exam. Tesuto suru = to try something out.

example.ja: 宿題、もう全部終わったの？
example.english: Have you finished all your homework already?

examplePolite.romaji: shukudai wa mou zenbu owarimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 宿題はもう全部終わりましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you finished all your homework?

items.notes: At work, shukudai ni sasete kudasai = let me take that away and get back to you.

items.use: A homeroom group within a school year, named by number or letter.

example.romaji: futari wa onaji kumi datta no?
example.ja: 二人は同じ組だったの？
example.english: Were you two in the same class?

examplePolite.romaji: futari wa onaji kumi datta n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 二人は同じ組だったんですか？
examplePolite.english: Were you two in the same class?

items.notes: Kurasu is more common for a school class today. In compounds it becomes -gumi: futarigumi = a pair, a duo.

items.use: For handing in homework, reports or forms, usually by a deadline.

example.ja: レポート、もう提出した？
example.english: Did you hand in the report yet?

examplePolite.romaji: repooto wa mou teishutsu shimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: レポートはもう提出しましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you submitted the report yet?

items.notes: Casually people often just say dasu: shukudai dashita? Teishutsu sounds more official.

blocks.label: Skills and expertise
blocks.rationale: Say what you research, specialise in or work with.
blocks.interference: Kenkyuu is research, not everyday studying (benkyou).

items.use: Serious study at a university or lab; kenkyuu suru = to research.

example.romaji: daigaku de nani kenkyuu shiteru no?
example.ja: 大学で何研究してるの？
example.english: What are you researching at university?

examplePolite.romaji: daigaku de nani o kenkyuu shite iru n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 大学で何を研究しているんですか？
examplePolite.english: What do you research at university?

items.notes: Studying for school or a test is benkyou, not kenkyuu.

items.use: Technical know-how, from a craftsperson's skill to a company's tech.

example.romaji: ano hito no gijutsu wa hontou ni sugoi yo.
example.ja: あの人の技術は本当にすごいよ。
example.english: That person's skills are seriously impressive.

examplePolite.romaji: ano kata no gijutsu wa hontou ni sugoi desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの方の技術は本当にすごいですね。
examplePolite.english: Their skills are truly impressive.

items.notes: It sounds technical; for 'he's good at it' people just say umai or jouzu.

items.use: Your field of work or study; also what a shop or school specialises in.

example.romaji: sore wa boku no senmon ja nai kara wakaranai.
example.ja: それは僕の専門じゃないから分からない。
example.english: That's not my field, so I don't know.

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa watashi no senmon ja nai node, wakarimasen.
examplePolite.ja: それは私の専門じゃないので、分かりません。
examplePolite.english: That's not my area, so I'm afraid I don't know.

items.notes: Senmon gakkou = vocational college; senmonka = specialist.

items.use: A computer system at work, or how a place is set up, like how a bar charges or how ordering works.

example.romaji: kono mise, dou iu shisutemu na no?
example.ja: この店、どういうシステムなの？
example.english: How does it work at this place?

examplePolite.romaji: kono mise wa dou iu shisutemu desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: この店はどういうシステムですか？
examplePolite.english: How does it work here?

items.notes: Shisutemu shougai = a system failure.

blocks.label: Doctors and medicine
blocks.rationale: Get help for an illness: medicine, doctors, tests and treatment.
blocks.interference: Kensa is a medical test, not a school tesuto.

items.use: You 'drink' medicine in Japanese, even pills: kusuri o nomu.

example.romaji: kusuri nonde, hayaku neta hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: 薬飲んで、早く寝た方がいいよ。
example.english: Take some medicine and get to bed early.

examplePolite.romaji: kusuri o nonde, hayaku neta hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 薬を飲んで、早く寝た方がいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You should take some medicine and go to bed early.

items.notes: Kusuriya or yakkyoku = pharmacy. In crime talk it can mean illegal drugs.

items.use: The friendly everyday word; isha alone sounds blunt, and you address a doctor as sensei.

example.romaji: ichido oishasan ni mite moratta hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: 一度お医者さんに診てもらった方がいいよ。
example.english: You should get a doctor to take a look.

examplePolite.romaji: ichido oishasan ni mite moratta hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 一度お医者さんに診てもらった方がいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You should have a doctor look at it.

items.notes: People often say byouin ni iku (go to the clinic) for 'see a doctor'.

items.use: Tests at a hospital, or checks on goods and bags; kensa o ukeru = have tests done.

example.romaji: ashita, byouin de kensa ga aru n da.
example.ja: 明日、病院で検査があるんだ。
example.english: I've got some tests at the hospital tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita, byouin de kensa o ukemasu.
examplePolite.ja: 明日、病院で検査を受けます。
examplePolite.english: I'm having some tests at the hospital tomorrow.

items.notes: Kensa no kekka = test results. A school test is tesuto, not kensa.

items.use: Ongoing care for an illness or injury, including dental work.

example.romaji: ima, ha no chiryou ni kayotteru.
example.ja: 今、歯の治療に通ってる。
example.english: I'm going in regularly for dental work right now.

examplePolite.romaji: ima, ha no chiryou ni kayotte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今、歯の治療に通っています。
examplePolite.english: I'm getting dental treatment at the moment.

items.notes: Chiryou o ukeru = get treatment. Naoru (to heal) is the result you hope for.

items.use: Means both the person and the clinic: haisha ni iku = go to the dentist.

example.romaji: ha ga itai kara, ashita haisha ni iku n da.
example.ja: 歯が痛いから、明日歯医者に行くんだ。
example.english: My tooth hurts, so I'm going to the dentist tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: ha ga itai node, ashita haisha ni ikimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 歯が痛いので、明日歯医者に行きます。
examplePolite.english: I have a toothache, so I'm going to the dentist tomorrow.

items.notes: Haisha-san is the softer, everyday form.

blocks.label: In and out of hospital
blocks.rationale: Share news about hospital stays, operations, recovery and pregnancy.
blocks.interference: Nyuuin (go in) and taiin (come out) are easy to swap.

items.english: to go into hospital; to be hospitalised
items.use: As a patient staying overnight or longer; nyuuin shite iru = is in hospital.

example.romaji: sobo ga kinou kara nyuuin shiteru n da.
example.ja: 祖母が昨日から入院してるんだ。
example.english: My grandma's been in hospital since yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: sobo ga kinou kara nyuuin shite iru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 祖母が昨日から入院しているんです。
examplePolite.english: My grandmother has been in hospital since yesterday.

items.notes: Opposite: taiin suru. Just seeing a doctor is byouin ni iku.

items.english: to leave hospital; to be discharged

example.ja: 母、来週退院できるって。
example.english: They say Mum can leave hospital next week.

examplePolite.romaji: haha wa raishuu taiin dekiru sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 母は来週退院できるそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear my mother can leave hospital next week.

items.notes: Opposite of nyuuin suru. Taiin omedetou = congrats on getting out of hospital.

items.use: The patient 'receives' it (shujutsu o ukeru), though casually people say shujutsu suru too.

example.romaji: raigetsu, hiza no shujutsu suru n da.
example.ja: 来月、膝の手術するんだ。
example.english: I'm having knee surgery next month.

examplePolite.romaji: raigetsu, hiza no shujutsu o ukemasu.
examplePolite.ja: 来月、膝の手術を受けます。
examplePolite.english: I'm having knee surgery next month.

items.notes: Shujutsu wa seikou shita = the operation went well.

items.use: A bit formal; for your own cold people usually say yoku naru or naoru.

example.romaji: kare, daibu kaifuku shita mitai da yo.
example.ja: 彼、だいぶ回復したみたいだよ。
example.english: He seems a lot better now.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa daibu kaifuku shita you desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼はだいぶ回復したようです。
examplePolite.english: He seems to have recovered quite a bit.

items.notes: Also used for the weather, the economy, or HP in games.

items.use: Ninshin shite iru = is pregnant.

example.ja: 実は、妊娠したの。
example.english: Actually... I'm pregnant.

examplePolite.romaji: jitsu wa, ninshin shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 実は、妊娠しました。
examplePolite.english: Actually, I'm pregnant.

items.notes: Ninshin gokagetsu = five months pregnant.

blocks.label: Big topics
blocks.rationale: Talk about the environment, history and education.
blocks.interference: None.

items.use: Both the natural environment and the conditions where you live, work or study.

example.romaji: ima no shokuba, kankyou ii yo.
example.ja: 今の職場、環境いいよ。
example.english: My current workplace is a really nice environment.

examplePolite.romaji: ima no shokuba wa kankyou ga ii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今の職場は環境がいいです。
examplePolite.english: My current workplace is a good environment.

items.notes: Kankyou mondai = environmental issues. Kankyou ga kawaru = your surroundings change, like a new job or school.

example.romaji: kono machi, kekkou rekishi aru n da yo.
example.ja: この町、結構歴史あるんだよ。
example.english: This town actually has quite a bit of history.

examplePolite.romaji: kono machi wa kekkou rekishi ga aru n desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: この町は結構歴史があるんですよ。
examplePolite.english: This town has quite a long history.

items.notes: Rekishi ga aru = have a long history. Also the school subject.

items.use: Schooling and bringing up children; at work, training new staff.

example.romaji: kodomo no kyouiku tte, okane kakaru yo ne.
example.ja: 子どもの教育って、お金かかるよね。
example.english: Kids' education really costs money, doesn't it?

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo no kyouiku wa okane ga kakarimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 子どもの教育はお金がかかりますね。
examplePolite.english: Children's education is expensive, isn't it?

items.notes: Kyouiku suru = to educate or train someone. Shinjin kyouiku = training new hires.

blocks.label: Celebrations and events
blocks.rationale: Talk about celebrating, weddings and events you're going to.
blocks.interference: Oiwai is the celebration or gift; omedetou is what you say.

items.use: Covers both the party and the gift or money you give.

example.ja: 誕生日のお祝いしようよ。
example.english: Let's celebrate your birthday.

examplePolite.romaji: tanjoubi no oiwai o shimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 誕生日のお祝いをしましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's celebrate your birthday.

items.notes: Oiwai suru = to celebrate. What you actually say to the person is omedetou.

example.romaji: raigetsu, tomodachi no kekkonshiki ni iku n da.
example.ja: 来月、友達の結婚式に行くんだ。
example.english: I'm going to a friend's wedding next month.

examplePolite.romaji: raigetsu, tomodachi no kekkonshiki ni ikimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 来月、友達の結婚式に行きます。
examplePolite.english: I'm going to a friend's wedding next month.

items.notes: Kekkon alone is marriage; -shiki makes it the ceremony. Guests give cash, called goshuugi.

items.use: Concerts, fan meetups, festivals, in-store promotions.

example.ja: 今度の土曜日、イベント行かない？
example.english: Want to go to an event this Saturday?

examplePolite.romaji: kondo no doyoubi, ibento ni ikimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今度の土曜日、イベントに行きませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like to go to an event this Saturday?

blocks.label: Trips away
blocks.rationale: Plan a trip: bags, souvenirs, hot springs.
blocks.interference: Ryokou is an ordinary trip; tabi is a more emotional journey.

example.ja: 夏休み、どこか旅行行かない？
example.english: Want to go on a trip somewhere over the summer break?

examplePolite.romaji: natsuyasumi ni dokoka ryokou ni ikimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 夏休みにどこか旅行に行きませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like to take a trip somewhere over the summer break?

items.notes: Goes with iku: ryokou ni iku. A business trip is shutchou, not ryokou.

items.use: Anything you carry or have delivered.

example.ja: 重いでしょ、荷物持つよ。
example.english: That's heavy, right? I'll take your bags.

examplePolite.romaji: omoi deshou, nimotsu mochimashou ka?
examplePolite.ja: 重いでしょう、荷物持ちましょうか？
examplePolite.english: That looks heavy. Shall I carry your bags?

items.notes: A delivery is also nimotsu: nimotsu ga todoita (a parcel came).

items.english: souvenir; gift brought back from a trip
items.use: Usually snacks brought back for family, friends or coworkers, or a small gift when visiting.

example.romaji: kore, kyouto no omiyage. minna de tabete.
example.ja: これ、京都のお土産。みんなで食べて。
example.english: This is from Kyoto. Share it with everyone.

examplePolite.romaji: kore, kyouto no omiyage desu. minasan de douzo.
examplePolite.ja: これ、京都のお土産です。皆さんでどうぞ。
examplePolite.english: This is from Kyoto. Please share it, everyone.

items.use: Both the spring and the bath or town built around it.

example.ja: 週末、温泉でも行きたいな。
example.english: I'd love to go to a hot spring this weekend.

examplePolite.romaji: shuumatsu wa onsen ni demo ikitai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 週末は温泉にでも行きたいですね。
examplePolite.english: I'd love to go to a hot spring this weekend.

items.notes: Onsen ni hairu = take a dip. A town bathhouse without spring water is a sentou.

items.use: More emotional and bookish than ryokou; used for long or solo trips, and in songs and titles.

example.romaji: itsuka hitori de tabi shite mitai na.
example.ja: いつか一人で旅してみたいな。
example.english: I'd love to travel on my own someday.

examplePolite.romaji: itsuka hitori de tabi o shite mitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: いつか一人で旅をしてみたいです。
examplePolite.english: I'd like to travel on my own someday.

items.notes: For a normal holiday trip, ryokou is the safe word.

blocks.label: Ways to get around
blocks.rationale: Say how you get somewhere: by train, bus, bike or taxi.
blocks.interference: Basu (bus) also turns up as bath in loanwords like basutaoru.

items.use: The everyday word for trains, including the subway.

example.ja: 電車遅れてるから、ちょっと遅れる。
example.english: The train's delayed, so I'll be a bit late.

examplePolite.romaji: densha ga okurete iru node, sukoshi okuremasu.
examplePolite.ja: 電車が遅れているので、少し遅れます。
examplePolite.english: The train is delayed, so I'll be a little late.

items.notes: Get on is densha ni noru, get off is oriru. The bullet train is shinkansen.

example.romaji: eki made basu de ikou ka.
example.ja: 駅までバスで行こうか。
example.english: Shall we take the bus to the station?

examplePolite.romaji: eki made basu de ikimashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: 駅までバスで行きましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we take the bus to the station?

items.notes: Basu also means bath in loanwords like basutaoru (bath towel); a bath itself is ofuro.

example.romaji: gakkou made jitensha de juppun gurai.
example.ja: 学校まで自転車で10分ぐらい。
example.english: It's about ten minutes to school by bike.

examplePolite.romaji: gakkou made jitensha de juppun gurai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 学校まで自転車で10分ぐらいです。
examplePolite.english: It's about ten minutes to school by bike.

items.notes: Casually called chari; a city bike with a basket is a mamachari.

example.romaji: mou osoi shi, takushii de kaerou.
example.ja: もう遅いし、タクシーで帰ろう。
example.english: It's late, let's take a taxi home.

examplePolite.romaji: mou osoi node, takushii de kaerimashou.
examplePolite.ja: もう遅いので、タクシーで帰りましょう。
examplePolite.english: It's late, so let's take a taxi home.

items.notes: Goes with noru (ride) and yobu (call): takushii o yobu.

blocks.label: Nature and animals
blocks.rationale: Talk about the outdoors, rivers and animals.
blocks.interference: Kawa also means skin or leather.

items.use: Shizen ni also means naturally, without forcing it.

example.romaji: inaka wa shizen ga ookute ii ne.
example.ja: 田舎は自然が多くていいね。
example.english: The countryside's nice, there's so much nature.

examplePolite.romaji: inaka wa shizen ga ookute ii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 田舎は自然が多くていいですね。
examplePolite.english: The countryside is nice, with so much nature.

items.notes: Shizen na = natural, as in shizen na kanji (a natural feel).

example.romaji: kawa no hou made sanpo shiyou ka.
example.ja: 川のほうまで散歩しようか。
example.english: Shall we walk down to the river?

examplePolite.romaji: kawa no hou made sanpo shimashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: 川のほうまで散歩しましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we take a walk down to the river?

items.notes: Kawa also means skin or leather; context tells them apart.

example.romaji: doubutsu suki? uchi, inu katteru yo.
example.ja: 動物好き？うち、犬飼ってるよ。
example.english: Do you like animals? We've got a dog.

examplePolite.romaji: doubutsu wa suki desu ka? uchi wa inu o katte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 動物は好きですか？うちは犬を飼っています。
examplePolite.english: Do you like animals? We have a dog.

items.notes: Doubutsuen is a zoo.

blocks.label: Sky and scenery
blocks.rationale: Point out the sky, stars, blossoms and a good view.
blocks.interference: None.

example.ja: 見て、空がすごいきれい。
example.english: Look, the sky's so pretty.

examplePolite.romaji: mite kudasai, sora ga sugoku kirei desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 見てください、空がすごくきれいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Look, the sky is really beautiful.

example.romaji: koko, hoshi ga yoku mieru ne.
example.ja: ここ、星がよく見えるね。
example.english: You can really see the stars here.

examplePolite.romaji: koko wa hoshi ga yoku miemasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: ここは星がよく見えますね。
examplePolite.english: You can really see the stars here.

items.notes: Also star ratings: hoshi mittsu = three stars.

items.use: The spring blossom everyone goes out to see; ohanami is the picnic under it.

example.ja: 桜、もう咲いてるね。
example.english: The cherry blossoms are already out.

examplePolite.romaji: sakura ga mou saite imasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 桜がもう咲いていますね。
examplePolite.english: The cherry blossoms are already out.

items.notes: Sakura ga saku = they bloom; chiru = they fall.

items.use: The view in front of you, usually a nice one.

example.romaji: koko kara no keshiki, saikou da ne.
example.ja: ここからの景色、最高だね。
example.english: The view from here is amazing.

examplePolite.romaji: koko kara no keshiki wa saikou desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: ここからの景色は最高ですね。
examplePolite.english: The view from here is wonderful.

blocks.label: Types and levels
blocks.rationale: Talk about kinds of things, sets and how good something is.
blocks.interference: Taipu and shurui both mean 'kind'; only taipu means 'my type'.

items.use: Very often the kind of person you're attracted to.

example.ja: 彼、全然タイプじゃない。
example.english: He's not my type at all.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa zenzen taipu ja arimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は全然タイプじゃありません。
examplePolite.english: He's not my type at all.

items.notes: Donna taipu ga suki? = What's your type?

example.ja: レベル高すぎてついていけない。
example.english: The level's too high, I can't keep up.

examplePolite.romaji: reberu ga takasugite, tsuite ikemasen.
examplePolite.ja: レベルが高すぎて、ついていけません。
examplePolite.english: The level is too high for me to keep up.

items.notes: Reberu ga takai = high standard, really good.

example.ja: いろんな種類があるね。
example.english: There are lots of kinds.

examplePolite.romaji: iroiro na shurui ga arimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: いろいろな種類がありますね。
examplePolite.english: There are many different kinds.

items.notes: Counts kinds directly: sanshurui = three kinds.

items.english: set (of things); meal set; setting up

example.romaji: setto de kau to yasui yo.
example.ja: セットで買うと安いよ。
example.english: It's cheaper if you buy them as a set.

examplePolite.romaji: setto de kau to yasui desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: セットで買うと安いですよ。
examplePolite.english: It's cheaper if you buy the set.

items.notes: Setto suru = set (an alarm) or set up; also a hair set at the salon.

blocks.label: Letters and numbers
blocks.rationale: Talk about writing, signatures, figures and how many.
blocks.interference: Ji and moji overlap; kazu is how many, suuji is the figure itself.

items.use: Often means someone's handwriting: ji ga kirei = neat handwriting.

example.ja: 字が小さくて読めない。
example.english: The writing's too small to read.

examplePolite.romaji: ji ga chiisakute yomemasen.
examplePolite.ja: 字が小さくて読めません。
examplePolite.english: The writing is too small for me to read.

items.notes: Kanji and kana are both ji.

items.use: A written character in any script, or text on a screen.

example.ja: この文字、なんて読むの？
example.english: How do you read this character?

examplePolite.romaji: kono moji wa nan to yomu n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: この文字は何と読むんですか？
examplePolite.english: How is this character read?

items.notes: Overlaps with ji, but moji never means handwriting.

items.use: The number as written or as data, not how many there are.

example.ja: この数字、間違ってない？
example.english: Isn't this number wrong?

examplePolite.romaji: kono suuji, machigatte imasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: この数字、間違っていませんか？
examplePolite.english: Isn't this figure wrong?

items.notes: For 'how many' use kazu; suuji is the figure itself.

items.use: How many there are: kazu ga ooi = there are a lot.

example.romaji: isu no kazu ga tarinai yo.
example.ja: 椅子の数が足りないよ。
example.english: There aren't enough chairs.

examplePolite.romaji: isu no kazu ga tarimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 椅子の数が足りません。
examplePolite.english: We don't have enough chairs.

items.notes: Kazoeru (to count) comes from the same root.

items.use: Sain suru = to sign; also a signal someone gives you.

example.ja: ここにサインしてくれる？
example.english: Can you sign here?

examplePolite.romaji: koko ni sain o onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: ここにサインをお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Please sign here.

items.notes: A shop or road sign is kanban or hyoushiki, not sain.

blocks.label: Next, last, the end
blocks.rationale: Say what comes next, what's last and when it's over.
blocks.interference: Tsuzuki is what follows; nokori is what's left.

items.english: what comes next; the rest; continuation
items.use: The next part of a story, show or task: tsuzuki wa ashita = the rest tomorrow.

example.ja: 続きが気になる！
example.english: I need to know what happens next!

examplePolite.romaji: tsuzuki ga ki ni narimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 続きが気になりますね。
examplePolite.english: I really want to know what happens next.

items.notes: From tsuzuku (to continue). Nokori is what's left over; tsuzuki is what follows.

items.use: A soft, slightly childlike way to say something is finished; also ends stories.

example.ja: 今日はこれでおしまい。
example.english: That's it for today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa kore de oshimai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日はこれでおしまいです。
examplePolite.english: That's all for today.

items.notes: Owari is the neutral 'end'; mou oshimai da can also mean 'it's all over for me'.

items.use: Mostly in compounds: saishuubi (last day), saishuukai (final episode).

example.ja: 明日が最終日だよ。
example.english: Tomorrow's the last day.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita ga saishuubi desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 明日が最終日ですよ。
examplePolite.english: Tomorrow is the final day.

items.notes: Saigo is the everyday 'last'; saishuu is for official endings.

items.english: in a row; consecutive; a series
items.use: Usually after a count: mikka renzoku = three days in a row.

example.romaji: mikka renzoku de zangyou da yo.
example.ja: 三日連続で残業だよ。
example.english: That's overtime three days in a row.

examplePolite.romaji: mikka renzoku de zangyou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 三日連続で残業です。
examplePolite.english: It's my third day in a row of overtime.

items.notes: Renzoku dorama = a TV drama series.

blocks.label: Where and which way
blocks.rationale: Ask and say where something is and which way to go.
blocks.interference: Ichi (position) sounds exactly like ichi (one).

example.ja: 駅はどっちの方向？
example.english: Which way is the station?

examplePolite.romaji: eki wa dochira no houkou desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 駅はどちらの方向ですか？
examplePolite.english: Which direction is the station?

items.notes: Houkou onchi = someone with no sense of direction.

items.use: Exactly where something is, as on a map or in a lineup.

example.ja: 今の位置、送ってくれる？
example.english: Can you send me your location?

examplePolite.romaji: ima no ichi o okutte moraemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今の位置を送ってもらえますか？
examplePolite.english: Could you send me your current location?

items.notes: Same sounds as ichi (one); pitch and context tell them apart.

items.use: The centre point, or the main focus: X o chuushin ni = centred on X.

example.ja: 町の中心に住んでる。
example.english: I live right in the centre of town.

examplePolite.romaji: machi no chuushin ni sunde imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 町の中心に住んでいます。
examplePolite.english: I live in the centre of town.

items.notes: Mannaka is the everyday 'middle'; chuushin also means the main part.

blocks.label: Top, biggest, only
blocks.rationale: Talk about the best, the biggest, huge amounts and the only one.
blocks.interference: Saidai is the biggest single thing; tairyou is a big amount.

items.english: top; first place; the head (of a group)

example.romaji: kanojo, kurasu de toppu nan da yo.
example.ja: 彼女、クラスでトップなんだよ。
example.english: She's top of the class.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo wa kurasu de toppu nan desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女はクラスでトップなんですよ。
examplePolite.english: She's top of her class.

items.notes: Rank or leader; the physical top of a thing is ue.

items.use: Usually before a noun with no: saidai no mondai = the biggest problem.

example.romaji: sore ga saidai no mondai da yo.
example.ja: それが最大の問題だよ。
example.english: That's the biggest problem.

examplePolite.romaji: sore ga saidai no mondai desu.
examplePolite.ja: それが最大の問題です。
examplePolite.english: That's the biggest problem.

items.notes: Opposite: saishou (smallest, minimum).

items.english: a large amount; loads; in bulk
items.use: Usually tairyou ni (in huge amounts) or tairyou no (a huge amount of).

example.ja: メールが大量に来てる。
example.english: I've got a ton of emails.

examplePolite.romaji: meeru ga tairyou ni kite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: メールが大量に来ています。
examplePolite.english: A huge number of emails have come in.

items.notes: Everyday talk often uses ippai instead.

items.use: Usually before a noun with no: yuiitsu no tomodachi = my only friend.

example.romaji: kore ga yuiitsu no shumi nan da.
example.ja: これが唯一の趣味なんだ。
example.english: This is my only hobby.

examplePolite.romaji: kore ga yuiitsu no shumi nan desu.
examplePolite.ja: これが唯一の趣味なんです。
examplePolite.english: This is my one and only hobby.

items.notes: Sounds a bit weighty; dake (only) is the everyday way.

blocks.label: Losing and missing out
blocks.rationale: Lets you react to a loss, a near miss, someone else's luck, or your own weakness.
blocks.interference: Kuyashii (gutted at losing) vs oshii (so close) vs nasakenai (pathetic).

items.use: The sting of losing or being beaten when you could have won; English has no single word for it.

example.romaji: ato chotto de kateta noni. kuyashii!
example.ja: あとちょっとで勝てたのに。悔しい！
example.english: We almost won. So frustrating!

examplePolite.romaji: ato chotto de kateta noni. kuyashii desu.
examplePolite.ja: あとちょっとで勝てたのに。悔しいです。
examplePolite.english: We almost won. It's really frustrating.

items.notes: Not regret over your own wrongdoing; that's koukai.

items.use: Said straight to someone, friendly not bitter: 'ii na, urayamashii!' = lucky you!

example.ja: ハワイ行くの？うらやましい！
example.english: You're going to Hawaii? I'm so jealous!

examplePolite.romaji: hawai ni iku n desu ka. urayamashii desu.
examplePolite.ja: ハワイに行くんですか。うらやましいです。
examplePolite.english: You're going to Hawaii? I'm jealous.

items.notes: Slang short form: urayama. Shitto is the darker, possessive jealousy.

items.use: Often aimed at yourself: 'nasakenai' = I'm so pathetic.

example.romaji: konna koto de naku nante, nasakenai na.
example.ja: こんなことで泣くなんて、情けないな。
example.english: Crying over something like this. How pathetic of me.

examplePolite.romaji: konna koto de naku nante, nasakenai desu.
examplePolite.ja: こんなことで泣くなんて、情けないです。
examplePolite.english: Crying over something like this. It's pathetic of me.

items.notes: Stronger than hazukashii (embarrassed): it's disappointment in weakness.

items.english: so close!; a shame; a waste
items.use: Shouted when someone just misses: 'oshii!' = so close!

example.ja: 惜しい！ほぼ合ってるけど、違う。
example.english: So close! Nearly right, but no.

examplePolite.romaji: oshii desu! hobo atte imasu kedo, chigaimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 惜しいです！ほぼ合っていますけど、違います。
examplePolite.english: So close! Nearly right, but not quite.

items.notes: Also for losing something good: yameru no wa oshii = it's a shame to quit. Mottainai is the word for wasting things.

blocks.label: All-in feelings
blocks.rationale: Lets you say you hate something, are hooked on it, can't resist it, or are giving it everything.
blocks.interference: Tamaranai can be praise (irresistible) or complaint (unbearable); hisshi (desperate effort) vs muchuu (absorbed).

items.use: The strong form of kirai; used freely for food and things, and in fights with people.

example.ja: ピーマン大嫌いなんだよ。
example.english: I hate green peppers.

examplePolite.romaji: piiman ga daikirai nan desu.
examplePolite.ja: ピーマンが大嫌いなんです。
examplePolite.english: I really hate green peppers.

items.notes: Grammar like suki: X ga daikirai. Opposite: daisuki.

items.use: Mostly as hisshi ni + verb: doing something with everything you've got.

example.ja: 今必死に勉強してる。
example.english: I'm studying like mad right now.

examplePolite.romaji: ima hisshi ni benkyou shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今必死に勉強しています。
examplePolite.english: I'm studying as hard as I can right now.

items.notes: Can tease: nani hisshi ni natteru no? = why so desperate?

items.english: hooked on; crazy about; absorbed in
items.use: Pattern X ni muchuu: 'geemu ni muchuu' = hooked on games.

example.romaji: ima kono anime ni muchuu nan da.
example.ja: 今このアニメに夢中なんだ。
example.english: I'm totally hooked on this anime right now.

examplePolite.romaji: ima kono anime ni muchuu nan desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今このアニメに夢中なんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm really into this anime right now.

items.notes: Muchuu de = so absorbed you lose track: muchuu de jikan o wasureta = I lost track of time.

items.use: Mostly praise for food, smells and cute things; after a te-form it means 'unbearably': atsukute tamaranai = unbearably hot.

example.ja: このカレーの匂い、たまらない。
example.english: The smell of this curry is irresistible.

examplePolite.romaji: kono karee no nioi, tamaranai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: このカレーの匂い、たまらないですね。
examplePolite.english: The smell of this curry is irresistible.

items.notes: Often shortened to tamannai in speech.

blocks.label: Looks and style
blocks.rationale: Lets you compliment how people look and what they wear.
blocks.interference: Kakkoii is cool, oshare is fashionable; oniai is for couples, niau for clothes.

items.use: Praise for looks (often men), clothes, cars, or a cool thing someone did.

example.ja: そのジャケット、かっこいいね。
example.english: That jacket looks cool.

examplePolite.romaji: sono jaketto, kakkoii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: そのジャケット、かっこいいですね。
examplePolite.english: That jacket looks cool.

items.notes: Past is kakkoyokatta. Opposite: kakkowarui = uncool, embarrassing. Also written カッコいい.

items.use: Often a compliment on looking young: 'wakai ne!' = you look so young!

example.ja: お母さん、すごく若いね！
example.english: Your mom looks so young!

examplePolite.romaji: okaasan, totemo wakai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: お母さん、とても若いですね。
examplePolite.english: Your mother looks very young.

items.notes: Wakai koro = when I was young. Wakaku mieru = look young.

items.use: For people, clothes and places: 'oshare na kafe' = a trendy café.

example.romaji: kyou no fuku, oshare da ne.
example.ja: 今日の服、おしゃれだね。
example.english: Your outfit looks stylish today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou no fuku, oshare desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日の服、おしゃれですね。
examplePolite.english: Your outfit looks stylish today.

items.notes: Oshare suru = dress up. Kakkoii is cool; oshare is fashionable.

items.use: Mostly about couples: 'oniai da ne' = you two are perfect together.

example.romaji: futari, honto ni oniai da ne.
example.ja: 二人、ほんとにお似合いだね。
example.english: You two make a really great couple.

examplePolite.romaji: ofutari, hontou ni oniai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: お二人、本当にお似合いですね。
examplePolite.english: You two make a really great couple.

items.notes: For clothes the verb niau is more common: niatteru = it suits you.

blocks.label: Strict, selfish and mean
blocks.rationale: Lets you complain about strict, selfish, unfair or mean people.
blocks.interference: Zurui (unfair, sly) vs ijiwaru (mean on purpose).

items.use: For strict people (parents, coaches) and tough conditions: 'kibishii na' = that's tough.

example.romaji: uchi no oya, kekkou kibishii n da yo.
example.ja: うちの親、けっこう厳しいんだよ。
example.english: My parents are pretty strict.

examplePolite.romaji: uchi no oya wa kekkou kibishii n desu.
examplePolite.ja: うちの親はけっこう厳しいんです。
examplePolite.english: My parents are pretty strict.

items.notes: Also for tight time or money: jikanteki ni kibishii = time is tight.

items.use: Someone who insists on getting their own way, like a spoiled child.

example.ja: もう、わがままばっかり言わないで。
example.english: Come on, stop being so demanding.

examplePolite.romaji: amari wagamama o iwanaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: あまりわがままを言わないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't be so demanding.

items.notes: Wagamama o iu = make selfish demands. Also humble: wagamama itte sumimasen = sorry to ask for something special.

items.use: The protest 'zurui!' when someone gets something you don't, or cheats; often half-joking.

example.romaji: hitori de zenbu tabeta no? zurui!
example.ja: 一人で全部食べたの？ずるい！
example.english: You ate it all by yourself? No fair!

examplePolite.romaji: hitori de zenbu tabeta n desu ka. zurui desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 一人で全部食べたんですか。ずるいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You ate it all by yourself? That's not fair.

items.notes: Zurui hito = a sly, sneaky person.

items.use: Deliberately unkind, often in small ways; also playful: 'ijiwaru!' = you meanie!

example.ja: そんな意地悪言わないでよ。
example.english: Don't be so mean.

examplePolite.romaji: sonna ijiwaru o iwanaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: そんな意地悪を言わないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't say such mean things.

items.notes: Ijiwaru suru = be mean to, tease. Ijimeru is harsher: real bullying.

blocks.label: Calm and careful
blocks.rationale: Lets you describe how calmly, carefully or eagerly someone works.
blocks.interference: Teinei (careful, polite) vs shinchou (cautious before deciding); shinchou also means height.

items.use: Often reisei ni: 'reisei ni natte' = calm down and think straight.

example.romaji: chotto matte, reisei ni natte yo.
example.ja: ちょっと待って、冷静になってよ。
example.english: Hold on, calm down.

examplePolite.romaji: chotto matte, reisei ni natte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっと待って、冷静になってください。
examplePolite.english: Hold on, please calm down.

items.notes: Ochitsuite is the everyday 'calm down'; reisei is about thinking clearly.

items.use: Usually shinchou ni: think it through before you decide or act.

example.romaji: kore wa shinchou ni kimeta hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: これは慎重に決めたほうがいいよ。
example.english: You should decide this one carefully.

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa shinchou ni kimeta hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: これは慎重に決めたほうがいいですよ。
